"The issue of territories is a red line that can be discussed exclusively at the level of leaders," Zelenskiy said.

item.title: Browns defeat Titans with third walkoff FG this season
item.description: Cleveland kicker Andre Szmyt made up for an earlier miss by nailing the game-winner from 32 yards on the final play of Sunday afternoon's 27-24 victory over the Tennessee Titans in Nashville, Tenn.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Cleveland kicker Andre Szmyt made up for an earlier miss by nailing the game-winner from 32 yards on the final play of Sunday afternoon's 27-24 victory over the Tennessee Titans in Nashville, Tenn. After Tennessee tied it 24-24 with 58 seconds remaining on Tony Pollard's third touchdown of the day, Deshaun Watson hit Harold Fannin Jr. for 36 yards with 28 seconds left. Szmyt, who missed from 43 yards in the fourth quarter, booted the winner to keep the Browns (5-2) atop the AFC North. Watson eclipsed 300 yards for the first time with the Browns as he completed 25 of 36 passes for 308 yards and an interception. He also rushed for a score. Quinshon Judkins carried 17 times for 96 yards with two scores. KC Concepcion had eight receptions for 129 yards. The Titans (1-6) came in off a 26-20 road win over Indianapolis and saw Cam Ward go 20-for-31 for 181 yards and an interception. Pollard carried 25 times for 129 yards. The Titans scored on their opening series for the first time this season as Pollard carried five times for 60 yards, which included 36 yards for a score. Cor'Dale Flott's 14-yard interception return set up the Titans again. Pollard capitalized on a toss sweep from 10 yards out to double the advantage at 8:35, the second rushing score against a Browns defense that had surrendered just one in 2026. Judkins had a 5-yard touchdown run with 5:32 left in the first quarter. Cleveland kept it a one-score game by stuffing Pollard on fourth down at the 1 with 9:34 left in the half. The teams exchanged turnovers as Cleveland's Denzel Ward picked off Cam Ward after a Browns fumble, which set up Judkins' second rushing score from 6 yards out at 2:17. Szmyt's 28-yard field goal on the half's final play put the Browns up 17-14. The visitors were unable to add on in the first minute of the fourth after Szmyt's errant 43-yard attempt. However, the Titans' Joey Slye evened it at 17 with a 29-yard kick with 8:41 left. The Browns engineered a 71-yard drive, highlighted by Dylan Sampson's 19-yard run and Concepcion's 18-yard reception that set up Watson's keeper from 9 yards out for the 24-17 lead with 4:34 left. Ward answered by leading the Titans on a 63-yard march capped by Pollard's 1-yard plunge with 58 seconds left for the tie. --Field Level Media

item.title: Bengals use big second-half rally to roll past Ravens
item.description: Joe Burrow threw four second-half touchdown passes and the Cincinnati Bengals scored 35 unanswered points to record a 35-13 victory over the host Baltimore Ravens on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Joe Burrow threw four second-half touchdown passes and the Cincinnati Bengals scored 35 unanswered points to record a 35-13 victory over the host Baltimore Ravens on Sunday. Burrow completed 16 of 18 passes for 249 yards while leading five touchdown drives in the half as Cincinnati (4-2) overcame a 13-0 halftime deficit to stun the Ravens (4-3). Overall, he was 22-for-30 passing for 292 yards. Tee Higgins caught six passes for 148 yards and a touchdown. Ja'Marr Chase, Mike Gesicki and Drew Sample also caught touchdown passes and Samaje Perine rushed for a score for the Bengals. Two-time NFL MVP Lamar Jackson (ankle) missed his third straight game for the Ravens. Tyler "Snoop" Huntley again drew the start and completed 23 of 34 passes for a career-high 298 yards. He threw one touchdown and one interception. Zay Flowers had eight catches for 137 yards and one score for Baltimore, which blew a double-digit lead for the second straight week. The Ravens have been outscored 48-0 over their last two second halves. The Cleveland Browns outscored them 13-0 last Sunday after the Ravens went up 10-0 at the half. Cincinnati got on the board with 9:24 remaining in the third quarter as Burrow's 6-yard scoring throw to Gesicki capped a nine-play, 66-yard drive. The Bengals took the lead less than five minutes later when Burrow connected on a 13-yard touchdown pass to Higgins with 4:29 to play in the period. Baltimore passed on a potential go-ahead field goal at the start of the fourth quarter. The Ravens instead went for it on fourth-and-2 from the Cincinnati 12, but Huntley's pass to tight end Josh Cuevas was incomplete. The Bengals answered by driving 88 yards in six plays. Burrow hit Higgins for 44 yards and Perine later scored on a 1-yard run to give Cincinnati a 21-13 lead with 11:14 left in regulation. The Bengals continued their comeback on the next drive as Burrow hit Chase for 30 yards and Higgins for 43 on back-to-back plays to move to the Baltimore 6. Three plays later, Burrow hit Chase for a 2-yard scoring pass to make it a 15-point margin, 28-13. On Baltimore's next play, Huntley's pass was deflected and Cincinnati's Demetrius Knight corralled the ball for an interception. Knight returned it 14 yards to the Ravens 24-yard line. Three plays later, Burrow tossed a 16-yard scoring pass to Sample to make it 35-13 with 6:21 left. Baltimore started fast, scoring on its fourth play from scrimmage. Huntley threw to his right to Flowers at the line of scrimmage, and Flowers broke free for a 48-yard catch-and-run touchdown. The Ravens tacked on two Tyler Loop field goals in the second quarter after long possessions that stalled. A drive of 78 yards on 18 plays that lasted 11 minutes ended with a 34-yard field goal, and a 13-play, 82-yard drive that lasted 6:09 led to a 24-yarder with 50 seconds left. Cincinnati possessed the ball for just 7:40 in the first half while being outgained 258-59. --Field Level Media

item.title: Supremo Tribunal Federal de Brasil amplía en dos horas horario de votación en balotaje presidencial
item.description: El magistrado del Supremo Tribunal Federal de Brasil Cristiano Zanin ordenó el domingo que se ampliara en dos horas el horario de votación de la segunda vuelta de las elecciones, accediendo a una solicitud de la campaña del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El magistrado del Supremo Tribunal Federal de Brasil Cristiano Zanin ordenó el domingo que se ampliara en dos horas el horario de votación de la segunda vuelta de las elecciones, accediendo a una solicitud de la campaña del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. En un principio, estaba previsto que las urnas cerraran a las 17:00 hora de Brasilia (2000 GMT). La campaña de Lula denunció que las autoridades de varias ciudades estaban restringiendo el acceso de los votantes al transporte público. En tanto, la autoridad electoral del país anunció que suspendía el recuento de los sufragios hasta que se cumpla el horario ampliado de la votación.

item.title: Billionaire Trump backer says Ben-Gvir, Smotrich should not serve in next Israeli government
item.description: The founder of Pershing Square Capital Management, who praised Netanyahu last week, said a government without the two ministers would send a message that Israel was "turning a new page."
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

Billionaire Trump backer says Ben-Gvir, Smotrich should not serve in next Israeli government

The founder of Pershing Square Capital Management, who praised Netanyahu last week, said a government without the two ministers would send a message that Israel was "turning a new page."

People walk near election banners with images of Israel's National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, leader of the Jewish Power (Otzma Yehudit) party, and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, leader of the Religious Zionist Party, in Sderot, near Israel's border with Gaza, in southern Israel, Oct 18 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Amir Cohen/TPX IMAGES OF THE DAY)

JERUSALEM: Billionaire American investor Bill Ackman on Sunday (Oct 25) said that Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich should not serve in Israel's next government, saying the two far-right politicians had caused enormous damage to the country's reputation. The public intervention by the prominent hedge fund manager, who is Jewish, comes just two days before Israel's general election, in which polls show a tight race between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition and the opposition. Ackman wrote on X that from the perspective of someone who had an understanding of how Israel was perceived in the United States, "Ben-Gvir and Smotrich have caused Israel enormous reputational damage with their statements and actions." BOTH MINISTERS HAVE FACED SANCTIONS The founder of Pershing Square Capital Management, who praised Netanyahu last week, said a government without the two ministers would send a message that Israel was "turning a new page."

"This will allow Israel to rebuild lost credibility, increase the opportunity for an expansion of the Abraham Accords, and enjoy a better relationship with Democrats and Republicans and Americans at large," he said. The Abraham Accords are the 2020 agreement, mediated by President Donald Trump's first administration, that saw Israel establish relations with the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain. It later reestablished official ties with Morocco. Representatives for Ben-Gvir and Smotrich did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Related:

Thousands rally in Tel Aviv against Netanyahu ahead of vote

Middle East conflict: Israel faces pressure from Western allies over Gaza and West Bank

As ministers in Netanyahu's religious-nationalist coalition, Ben-Gvir and Smotrich have overseen policies widely perceived as discriminatory against Israel's minority Arab population and Palestinians living in the occupied West Bank. Several countries, including Britain, Canada and Australia, have imposed sanctions on the two ministers over accusations that they have incited violence against Palestinians in the West Bank. Ben-Gvir's Jewish Power party is projected to win around 10 parliamentary seats at Tuesday's election, up from 6, while Smotrich's Religious Zionism is projected to win 8, up from 7. Ackman, who was visiting Israel last week, and who along with his wife Neri Oxman owns 5 percent of the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, supported Donald Trump's candidacy for president in 2024. Trump last week publicly endorsed Netanyahu for prime minister. Nimrod Goren, the president of Israeli think tank Mitvim, said Ackman's statement appeared to reflect a desire among Trump's circles for Netanyahu to drop his far-right allies after the vote to form a 'unity government' with opposition parties. However, Gadi Eisenkot, the leading challenger to Netanyahu, and other opposition party leaders have ruled out forming a government with Israel's longest-serving prime minister. Speaking at a Tel Aviv conference on Thursday, Ackman praised Netanyahu, who he said had done a good job in protecting and defending Israel since the Oct 7 2023 Hamas attack. Thousands of Israelis rallied in Tel Aviv on Saturday calling for an independent inquiry into the attack that killed around 1,200 people.

Source: Reuters/fs

item.title: Terland strikes late to give Man United derby draw with City in WSL
item.description: Manchester United striker Elisabeth Terland scored a late equaliser to knock visitors Manchester City off top spot in the Women's Super League table on Sunday evening as a hotly contested derby finished 1-1 at the Leigh Sports Ground.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Manchester United striker Elisabeth Terland scored a late equaliser to knock visitors Manchester City off top spot in the Women's Super League table on Sunday evening as a hotly contested derby finished 1-1 at the Leigh Sports Ground. Reigning champions City dropped points for the first time this season, allowing Chelsea to go top on goal difference after they came back from a goal down to beat Crystal Palace 3-1 earlier in the day. Chelsea and City both have 19 points, with London City Lionesses third on 16 and Manchester United fourth on 11. Making her 100th WSL appearance, Bunny Shaw gave City the lead in the 66th minute, brushing off the challenge of Dominique Janssen and rattling a shot into the far corner to break the deadlock and silence the home fans, who booed and heckled her throughout. The game looked to be getting away from United until a well-worked freekick was lofted into the box in the 89th minute, and Norway international Terland was on hand to blast the ball into the net to grab a point for her side. On Merseyside, Liverpool's Jana Fernandez Velasco struck deep into stoppage time to snatch a 2-2 draw at home to London City. Aston Villa raced out to a 3-0 lead over Everton by the 50th minute with Amalie Vangsgaard scoring twice, but the home side scored twice late on to ensure a nervous finish as Villa held on for a 3-2 win. Charlton Athletic's miserable run continued as they slumped to their seventh straight defeat. Substitute Wilma Leidhammar scored the only goal of the game for Birmingham City in the 68th minute to leave Charlton still firmly rooted to the bottom of the table and searching for their first point of the season.

item.title: Shadab heroics lift Pakistan past England in one-wicket thriller
item.description: Pakistan all-rounder Shadab Khan struck an unbeaten 113 and shared a record 89-run last-wicket stand with Haris Rauf as the hosts rallied from 154-9 to secure a one-wicket win over England in Lahore on Sunday and book their place in the tri-series final.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pakistan all-rounder Shadab Khan struck an unbeaten 113 and shared a record 89-run last-wicket stand with Haris Rauf as the hosts rallied from 154-9 to secure a one-wicket win over England in Lahore on Sunday and book their place in the tri-series final. Chasing 242 for victory, Pakistan appeared to be heading towards defeat after England's bowlers reduced them to 154-9 in the 34th over. However, Shadab launched a superb counter-attack and, with Rauf making an unbeaten seven off 19 balls, guided the hosts to victory with 17 balls to spare. Their 89-run partnership was the highest for the final wicket in a successful ODI run chase. Earlier, England were bowled out for 241 in 46.4 overs despite Ben Duckett's composed 105. Shaheen Shah Afridi led Pakistan's bowling effort with 4-46 to dismantle England's top order. The defeat was England's third successive loss in the tri-series after Sri Lanka completed the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history, reaching a target of 430 with one ball to spare. Afridi struck in the opening over to dismiss Tom Banton before removing Joe Root in the third over, while Jordan Cox fell to Haris Rauf as England slumped to 52-4. Ben Duckett and Sam Curran steadied the innings with a fifth-wicket partnership of 93. Curran made 42 before becoming Afridi's third victim. Jamie Overton helped take England past 200, while Gus Atkinson finished unbeaten on 36. Pakistan lost Fakhar Zaman and Babar Azam for 10 apiece before Saad Baig struck a brisk 32 off 22 balls and Salman Ali Agha made 26 to briefly revive the chase. Shadab Khan came to the crease in the 24th over with the hosts struggling at 103-6. Shadab, who struck 13 fours and five sixes, was given out lbw to Atkinson with 21 runs needed, but successfully reviewed the decision after replays showed an inside edge.

item.title: Malik Willis guides Dolphins past Jets for long-sought first win
item.description: Malik Willis threw two touchdown passes to rookie Caleb Douglas and ran for another to help the Miami Dolphins pick up their first win, beating the New York Jets 28-25 on Sunday in East Rutherford, N.J.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Malik Willis threw two touchdown passes to rookie Caleb Douglas and ran for another to help the Miami Dolphins pick up their first win, beating the New York Jets 28-25 on Sunday in East Rutherford, N.J. Willis completed 14 of 21 passes for 208 yards without an interception and rushed for 37 yards on eight attempts to help give head coach Jeff Hafley his first NFL victory. Willis' final run -- not counting two kneel-downs that followed -- was a 2-yard quarterback sneak on fourth-and-1 from the Jets' 49, which sealed the outcome as Miami converted with less than two minutes left and New York was out of timeouts. Ollie Gordon II ran for 103 yards and a touchdown on 25 carries as Miami (1-5) rushed for 156 yards overall. The ground game helped seal the result on its final drive of the fourth quarter. The Jets (2-5) lost for the fifth time in six games and lost their eighth consecutive game against an AFC East opponent. Geno Smith completed 23 of 30 passes for 287 yards, three touchdowns and one interception to lead the Jets. Smith's third touchdown pass was a 12-yarder to Mason Taylor, who caught five passes for 62 yards and two touchdowns. Smith connected with Taylor on a two-point conversion to cut the Dolphins' lead to three with 3:24 left. But the Dolphins ran out the clock by converting a pair of first downs, beginning with a 14-yard run by Gordon. Braelon Allen started again for injured running back Breece Hall and ran for 104 yards on 17 carries, also catching six passes for 30 yards. Omar Cooper Jr. caught five passes for 115 yards and a touchdown. The Dolphins scored touchdowns on their first two drives for the first time this season, and led a game for the first time all year following Willis' 7-yard touchdown pass to Douglas, who returned to action Sunday after missing Miami's prior three games with an ankle injury. The lead lasted 2:16 until the Jets answered with a 13-yard touchdown pass from Smith to Taylor. But the Dolphins responded with a 14-play, 60-yard drive capped by a 1-yard dive up the middle by Gordon to take a 14-7 lead. The Dolphins took a 28-17 edge with 4:55 left in the fourth when Willis found Douglas down the sideline for a 63-yard score, giving Miami its highest scoring output of the season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Musk diz que SpaceX captou US$40 bi em dívida para comprar GPUs
item.description: Elon Musk afirmou que a SpaceX captou US$40 bilhões por meio de dívida para a compra de unidades de processamento gráfico (GPUs), acrescentando que o status de grau de investimento da empresa e as receitas dos negócios de internet via satélite Starlink e de lançamentos espaciais ajudaram a preservar seu acesso ao crédito.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Elon Musk afirmou que a SpaceX (SPCX.O) captou US$40 bilhões por meio de dívida para a compra de unidades de processamento gráfico (GPUs), acrescentando que o status de grau de investimento da empresa e as receitas dos negócios de internet via satélite Starlink e de lançamentos espaciais ajudaram a preservar seu acesso ao crédito. "Trata-se principalmente de dívida resgatável para compras de GPUs que chegarão no primeiro e segundo trimestres. Não é um fator importante neste trimestre", disse Musk em uma publicação no X. (Reportagem de Anusha Shah em Bengaluru)

item.title: STF prorroga horário de votação em todo Brasil até 19h
item.description: O ministro Cristiano Zanin, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), determinou a prorrogação do horário de votação no segundo turno em todo país até as 19h deste domingo, segundo decisão publicada pela corte.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O ministro Cristiano Zanin, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), determinou a prorrogação do horário de votação no segundo turno em todo país até as 19h deste domingo, segundo decisão publicada pela corte. Zanin atendeu a pedido da campanha à reeleição do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) que apontou a falta de transporte público em algumas cidades. Inicialmente as seções eleitorais deveriam fechar às 17h.

item.title: Report: Dustin Johnson among LIV players seeking $100M+ from PIF
item.description: Two-time major champion Dustin Johnson is among more than 10 LIV golfers seeking a total of more than $100 million from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, The Athletic reported Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Two-time major champion Dustin Johnson is among more than 10 LIV golfers seeking a total of more than $100 million from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, The Athletic reported Sunday. The PIF funded LIV Golf with lucrative contracts and tournament purses from the league's debut in 2022 until April, when it announced it would withdraw its support. The group of golfers, which includes fellow two-time major champion Bubba Watson, is seeking payments due under their original LIV contracts or money owed through severance agreements. Three-time major champion Jon Rahm of Spain has already announced he will not return for the reconfigured tour, dubbed LIV 2.0. Tyrrell Hatton, Ian Poulter and Tom McKibbin also have announced in recent days that they will not return to LIV. LIV 2.0 set a Sunday deadline for players to commit to the league's new era. New investor BC Partners Credit has the ability to extend the deadline, according to the report. Johnson's lawyer, David Cornwell, who also represents the players pursuing the claims against LIV, told The Athletic that further proceedings will depend on how the PIF handles the end of the league's initial iteration. According to Cornwell, the players seeking payments relied on the PIF's promises to keep LIV viable. "The PIF was an honorable business partner until what we regard as its abandonment of LIV golfers," Cornwell told The Athletic. "Professional sports leagues and their player unions in the United States, along with sports organizations worldwide, should take notice: the PIF's treatment of LIV golfers may signal how it will treat professional athletes in other sports. How you do one thing is usually how you do everything." --Field Level Media

item.title: Buccaneers rout Panthers 43-13 in Baker Mayfield's return
item.description: Bucky Irving rushed for 106 yards and two touchdowns, Calijah Kancey returned a fumble 32 yards for a touchdown and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers blasted the mistake-prone Carolina Panthers 43-13 on Sunday afternoon in Charlotte.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Bucky Irving rushed for 106 yards and two touchdowns, Calijah Kancey returned a fumble 32 yards for a touchdown and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers blasted the mistake-prone Carolina Panthers 43-13 on Sunday afternoon in Charlotte. Baker Mayfield was back at quarterback for the Buccaneers (2-5) after missing three games with a dislocated right thumb and had an easy return while completing 7 of 11 passes for 64 yards and one touchdown. The Buccaneers, playing in their first NFC South matchup of the season, had a 33-6 halftime lead with Mayfield attempting only nine passes. The Panthers (3-3) committed four turnovers and missed an extra-point kick. Bryce Young was 14-of-27 passing for 163 yards with two interceptions and a touchdown, while losing a fumble. Irving's rushing output came on 24 carries. Sean Tucker also ran for a touchdown for Tampa Bay, scoring on a late 46-yard run that pushed the advantage to 43-6. Teammate Kenny Gainwell tacked on 88 rushing yards on 14 attempts. Tampa Bay finished the game with 258 rushing yards. The Buccaneers built a 17-0 lead by early in the second quarter, with Al-Quadin Muhammad's sack leading to Kancey's return for a touchdown. Young hooked up with Darren Waller for a 50-yard touchdown in the second quarter but the Panthers could not generate momentum. Tykee Smith blocked the ensuing point-after attempt and Zyon McCollum returned it the rest of the way for two Bucs points. The Buccaneers then drove 59 yards on eight plays for Irving's 1-yard TD run to make it 26-6. Three plays later, McCollum intercepted Young to put the Buccaneers at the Carolina 32. Tampa Bay converted on Mayfield's 14-yard touchdown pass to Tez Johnson with four seconds remaining in the half. Tampa Bay opened the scoring on the game's first possession, marching 70 yards with Irving running 4 yards for the touchdown. David Moore's muffed punt at the Carolina 18 set up the Buccaneers' next points. They scored on Chase McLaughlin's 22-yard field goal. Young threw a second-half interception that turned into McLaughlin's 44-yard field goal in the third quarter that gave the Buccaneers a 36-6 lead. Tampa Bay played without injured wide receiver Emeka Egbuka. --Field Level Media

item.title: Algeria to send troops to Niger in first foreign deployment since 1973
item.description: Algeria's parliament approved a resolution on Sunday authorising the deployment of army units to Niger, a parliamentary statement said, in what would mark Algeria's first foreign troop deployment since it sent forces to support Egypt in the 1973 war.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Algeria's parliament approved a resolution on Sunday authorising the deployment of army units to Niger, a parliamentary statement said, in what would mark Algeria's first foreign troop deployment since it sent forces to support Egypt in the 1973 war. Lawmakers unanimously backed the deployment of National Army units to Madama in northern Niger, near the Libyan border, at the site of a former French base used during Operation Barkhane, the statement said. No troops have been officially deployed yet, according to a Niger security source. But Niger presidential chief of staff General Bacharou Ibro Amadou has been visiting the Kawar area in the Bilma department of Agadez region since October 19. He travelled to Madama for talks with local military commanders before returning to Dirkou to meet military and traditional authorities on plans for the base. The move highlights a rapid improvement in ties between Algiers and Niamey after a period of strain. Algeria opposed the 2023 coup that brought Niger's current military leaders to power. Relations worsened last year, when Niger recalled its ambassador from Algiers after Algeria shot down a Malian drone near their border. Niger, Mali and Burkina Faso are all ruled by military leaders who seized power in coups and later formed the Alliance of Sahel States. Niger, like other countries in West Africa's Sahel region, is battling insurgents linked to al Qaeda and Islamic State. Algeria, which shares a border with Niger, has traditionally regarded stability in the Sahel-Sahara as a key regional security priority. Ties have improved this year. Niger President Abdourahamane Tiani visited Algiers in February, and Niger Defence Minister Salifou Mody travelled there on October 20 with a delegation of defence experts for talks on security cooperation. Algeria has also deepened its economic interests in Niger. State energy company Sonatrach is working with Niger and Nigeria on the Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline, which is intended to create a new export corridor for African gas to international markets, particularly Europe. Sonatrach said in 2022 that it had signed a production-sharing agreement with Niger's petroleum ministry for the Kafra region, where two exploration wells held proven reserves of 168 million barrels and 100 million barrels, respectively.

item.title: Musk says SpaceX raised $40 billion in debt deal, predicts neocloud shakeout
item.description: Elon Musk said on Sunday that SpaceX had closed $40 billion in debt financing for graphics processing units, underscoring the soaring cost of building AI computing capacity.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Elon Musk said on Sunday that SpaceX (SPCX.O) had closed $40 billion in debt financing for graphics processing units, underscoring the soaring cost of building AI computing capacity. Musk, in a post on X, attributed the successful debt raise to the company's investment-grade status and revenue from its Starlink satellite internet and launch businesses. It was not immediately clear from Musk’s post what he meant by the deal being “closed” or whether investors had agreed to pricing for the debt. "This is primarily callable debt for GPU purchases that will arrive in Q1 and Q2. Not a major factor this quarter," Musk said in the post. For the fourth quarter, the company expects $35 billion to $40 billion in capital expenditure, according to Chief Financial Officer Bret Johnsen. Reuters [USN:L6N45S1CR TEXT:"reported"] earlier this month that SpaceX was in talks with banks and asset managers to raise $40 billion for the purchase of Nvidia (NVDA.O) artificial intelligence chips. The funding highlights the enormous capital requirement of the AI boom, as technology companies race to secure advanced processors and build out the computing infrastructure needed to support AI development. Musk said debt markets "have almost entirely shut off access to money for any company that doesn’t have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers." As a result, he predicted neocloud companies would face significant consolidation and failures, and later said SpaceX won't buy any neoclouds, calling it “pointless.” Unlike larger cloud firms that serve a broad range of industries, neoclouds such as Nebius (NBIS.O) and CoreWeave (CRWV.O) mostly focus on tech customers and offer capacity tailored for AI technology. Investors have started betting [USN:L6N468125 TEXT:"against"] US neocloud and data center companies, after fears that their debt-fueled AI buildout was becoming unsustainable sparked a selloff. AI INVESTMENT, CHIP MANUFACTURING SpaceX's [USN:L4N4661M0 TEXT:"revenue climbed"] 161% from a year ago to $14.58 billion for the three months ended September 30. AI revenue surged by almost 10 times to $7.56 billion, the clearest evidence yet that SpaceX’s heavy investment in AI was paying off. The shift is reshaping a company whose financial engine has long been its Starlink satellite internet services business and whose longer-term ambitions still hinge on getting Starship rockets into regular service. Terafab, the chip manufacturing joint venture between SpaceX and Tesla (TSLA.O) in Austin, should produce its first test chip around May or June of next year as it aims to reach volume production by the third quarter of 2028. Musk told investors in a conference call last week that a merger of his two companies would be "a good idea," citing growing overlap between them. Prior to its blockbuster IPO, SpaceX [USN:L6N416023 TEXT:"listed"] "manufacturing our own GPUs" among the substantial capital expenditures it is undertaking in its S-1 statement, warning prospective investors of its big spending plans to develop AI and other technologies.

item.title: Oregon fires OC Drew Mehringer after loss to Illinois
item.description: Oregon fired first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer on Sunday, one day after the Ducks scored 10 points in a loss to Illinois and fell to 4-3 on the season.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Oregon fired first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer on Sunday, one day after the Ducks scored 10 points in a loss to Illinois and fell to 4-3 on the season. Head coach Dan Lanning announced the move Sunday morning. "This was a decision I felt was in the best interest of our football program, as I believe a new direction is necessary to move our offense forward," Lanning said. Mehringer, 38, joined Oregon in 2022 after coaching at New Mexico. He initially served as tight ends coach before adding co-offensive coordinator to his title last year. Lanning promoted him to offensive coordinator for the 2026 season after Will Stein left to become head coach at Kentucky. The Ducks' performance against Illinois in Champaign on Saturday proved to be the breaking point. Oregon (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) compiled 426 yards of total offense, including 180 rushing and 246 passing, but managed just a touchdown and a field goal in a 21-10 defeat. The Ducks were held scoreless in the second half as Illinois rallied for the victory. Oregon ranks sixth in the 18-team Big Ten in scoring at 33.1 points per game, but that average is boosted by an 84-point output against FCS opponent Portland State. The Ducks have averaged 14 points in their past three conference games after scoring 41 in their Big Ten opener against Southern California. Oregon played those three games without star quarterback Dante Moore, who has been sidelined with a concussion after taking an illegal hit to the head against Southern California. The Ducks rank 10th in the conference in rushing offense at 145.4 yards per game and fifth in passing offense at 277.7 yards per game. --Field Level Media

item.title: Vikings take over late to edge Colts, move to 6-0
item.description: Kyler Murray passed for 150 yards and a touchdown, and Minnesota Vikings safety Harrison Smith made an interception in the final minutes to preserve a 16-10 victory over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday afternoon in Minneapolis.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kyler Murray passed for 150 yards and a touchdown, and Minnesota Vikings safety Harrison Smith made an interception in the final minutes to preserve a 16-10 victory over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday afternoon in Minneapolis. T.J. Hockenson had a touchdown catch for Minnesota (6-0), which won its first game after a bye to remain unbeaten. Jordan Mason had a team-high 68 rushing yards, and Justin Jefferson caught four passes for 44 yards on seven targets. Jonathan Taylor rushed for 95 yards and a touchdown to lead Indianapolis (2-5). Daniel Jones completed 13 of 22 yards for 108 yards and an interception. Smith picked off Jones at the Vikings' 44-yard line with 1:08 remaining to spoil the Colts' final comeback attempt. The Vikings trailed for most of the game, only taking the lead early in the fourth quarter. Murray looked left and fired a pass to Hockenson, who reached the ball across the left pylon for the 5-yard touchdown. The extra effort put the Vikings on top 13-10 with 14:36 to play in the fourth quarter. Will Reichard made a 52-yard field goal to increase Minnesota's lead to 16-10 with 1:39 to go. The Colts opened the scoring on their first possession. Taylor took a pitch left, weaved through the line of scrimmage and outraced the Vikings' secondary for a 38-yard rushing touchdown with 9:13 to go in the first quarter. The play marked Taylor's eighth touchdown in seven games this season. The Vikings cut the deficit to 7-3 in the opening seconds of the second quarter when Reichard made a 28-yard field goal. Reichard struck again, this time from 47 yards, to pull the Vikings within 7-6 with 6:37 remaining in the first half. It was Reichard's 36th field goal in a row without a miss, which broke Gary Anderson's previous franchise record of 35 consecutive field goals in 1998. Spencer Shrader made a 43-yarder to boost the Colts' lead to 10-6 as time expired in the half. --Field Level Media

item.title: ATP roundup: Daniil Medvedev bags title No. 25 in Almaty
item.description: Top seed and defending champion Daniil Medvedev of Russia rallied past Georgian Nikoloz Basilashvili 6-7 (6), 6-1, 6-3 to claim the title at the Almaty Open on Sunday in Kazakhstan.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Top seed and defending champion Daniil Medvedev of Russia rallied past Georgian Nikoloz Basilashvili 6-7 (6), 6-1, 6-3 to claim the title at the Almaty Open on Sunday in Kazakhstan. Medvedev, the World No. 5, picked up his fourth tour-level title of 2026 and the 25th of his career. He smashed 22 aces to Basilashvili's three and had to gut out a three-setter after failing to polish off a set-point opportunity in the first-set tiebreaker. Basilashvili, who was seeking his sixth title and first since May 2021, saved 6 of 10 break points he faced but was unable to break Medvedev's serve on two tries. He committed twice as many unforced errors -- 40 to Medvedev's 20. Grand Prix Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes No. 6 seed Lorenzo Musetti of Italy took down No. 2 seed Taylor Fritz 6-3, 6-4 in the final in Lyon, France. Musetti captured his first ATP title in four years and his third overall. He played a far cleaner match than his counterpart, never facing break point and finishing with 11 unforced errors to Fritz's 28. Fritz was aiming for his 12th career ATP crown. It was a long-awaited breakthrough for Musetti, who enjoyed a run to the quarterfinals at the most recent Australian Open and lost the final of the 2025 Monte-Carlo Masters, an ATP 1000 event. Musetti had to save four match points against countryman and No. 1 seed Flavio Cobolli in the semifinals Saturday. BNP Paribas Fortis European Open Dutchman Tallon Griekspoor rallied from a dropped first set to defeat German Jan-Lennard Struff 4-6, 6-3, 6-4 and win the title in Brussels, Belgium. After going down a break in the first set and failing to catch up, Griekspoor broke Struff's serve in the eighth game of the second set and served out for the set. In similar fashion, the foes held serve through the first eight games of the final set until Struff went down 0-40 in the ninth game and could not recover. Griekspoor then served out for the championship. For the unseeded Griekspoor, it was his fourth career title and first of the season. Struff recorded more winners (39-37) but also more unforced errors (31-25). --Field Level Media

item.title: Zelenskiy diz que alertas dos EUA sobre ataques balísticos russos foram totalmente restabelecidos
item.description: O presidente da Ucrânia, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, afirmou que os alertas dos Estados Unidos sobre iminentes ataques russos com mísseis balísticos, considerados cruciais para as defesas aéreas ucranianas, foram totalmente restabelecidos após problemas recentes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente da Ucrânia, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, afirmou que os alertas dos Estados Unidos sobre iminentes ataques russos com mísseis balísticos, considerados cruciais para as defesas aéreas ucranianas, foram totalmente restabelecidos após problemas recentes. Em entrevista ao canal de televisão ucraniano TSN, Zelenskiy disse que o serviço de internet via satélite Starshield, da SpaceX (SPCX.O) , voltou a funcionar desde as primeiras horas da manhã de sábado com velocidades de até 420 quilômetros por hora, após ter sua capacidade reduzida no início de outubro em meio à pressão diplomática de Washington sobre Kiev. (Reportagem de Max Hunder)

item.title: Report: Contenders considering offer for Colts RB Jonathan Taylor
item.description: The Green Bay Packers, Seattle Seahawks, Denver Broncos and Minnesota Vikings are among the potential trade suitors for star running back Jonathan Taylor following the Indianapolis Colts' firing of general manager Chris Ballard, ESPN reported over the weekend.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Green Bay Packers, Seattle Seahawks, Denver Broncos and Minnesota Vikings are among the potential trade suitors for star running back Jonathan Taylor following the Indianapolis Colts' firing of general manager Chris Ballard, ESPN reported over the weekend. According to the report, the Colts (2-5) will wait to see how their next three games unfold ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Following Sunday's 16-10 loss to Minnesota Vikings, Indianapolis visits the Jacksonville Jaguars next Sunday before returning home to face the Dallas Cowboys on Nov. 8. If the Colts are unable to turn their season around during that stretch, new chief of personnel Ed Dodds will work with owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon and the front office to devise a plan that could involve shifting resources toward the future, according to the report. Irsay-Gordon would prefer not to trade Taylor as part of a rebuild, per the report, but the possibility remains that the former first-team All-Pro could be playing elsewhere next month. Despite Taylor signing a two-year, $44 million contract extension in August, teams view the three-time Pro Bowl selection as a major trade target. Taylor, 27, is owed the remainder of his nearly $7 million base salary this season, followed by $16 million in 2027 and nearly $18 million in 2028. Entering Week 7, Taylor had rushed for 492 yards and seven touchdowns through the first six games of the season. He added 95 yards and the Colts' lone touchdown on 18 carries against Minnesota. In his seventh NFL season since the Colts selected him in the second round of the 2020 draft, Taylor has rushed for 8,185 yards and 77 touchdowns in 91 games (85 starts). He also has 204 receptions for 1,647 yards and seven receiving touchdowns. --Field Level Media

item.title: Bon Secours nears $6 billion takeover of Bain-backed Surgery Partners, FT reports
item.description: US based not-for-profit health system Bon Secours Mercy Health is in late-stage talks to buy a majority stake in Surgery Partners in a deal which would value the company at roughly $6 billion including debt, the Financial Times reported on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US based not-for-profit health system Bon Secours Mercy Health is in late-stage talks to buy a majority stake in Surgery Partners (SGRY.O) in a deal which would value the company at roughly $6 billion including debt, the Financial Times reported on Sunday. Here are a few details: The potential, deal which could be announced as early as Monday, values the short-stay surgery operator at about $20 a share, the report said, citing people familiar with the matter Bon Secours Mercy Health and Surgery Partners did not immediately respond to Reuters request for comment outside regular business hours Bain Capital, its largest shareholder, will retain its almost 40 per cent shareholding in Surgery Partners as part of the take-private deal, the report added The potential deal would represent a 25.8% premium to Surgery Partners' last close of $15.9, as per LSEG data. Surgery Partners rejected Bain Capital's take-private offer in June last year, saying it was unable to agree to the terms set by the private equity group

item.title: Inter strike late to keep pace with Lazio as Juve ease pressure with Lecce win
item.description: Inter Milan kept pace with Lazio at the top of Serie A after scoring twice in stoppage time to earn a 2–1 home win over Fiorentina on Sunday, while injury-hit Juventus halted their recent slump with a 2–0 victory at Lecce.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Inter Milan kept pace with Lazio at the top of Serie A after scoring twice in stoppage time to earn a 2–1 home win over Fiorentina on Sunday, while injury-hit Juventus halted their recent slump with a 2–0 victory at Lecce. Fiorentina had looked set to inflict Inter's first league defeat of the season through a second-half goal from Alex Jimenez before Marcus Thuram equalised in stoppage time. Minutes later, Thuram was brought down in the penalty area by Victor Valdepenas, allowing Piotr Zielinski to convert the resulting spot-kick and seal all three points for the hosts. The late turnaround leaves Inter level on 22 points with Lazio, who won 2–1 at [USN:L2N46A049 TEXT:"home against Parma"] on Saturday, while AS Roma are third on 18 points. Fiorentina's third consecutive league defeat means they remain 18th with four points. Juventus and their coach Luciano Spalletti gained much-needed respite with their win at the Stadio Via del Mare, despite having only seven outfield players on the bench. Weston McKennie opened the scoring in the 29th minute with a freekick that floated over the wall, before Douglas Luiz drove in a precise low shot from outside the box shortly before the break. Juve controlled the rest of the match, with Lecce's frustration eventually boiling over when Kialonda Gaspar was shown a red card with the final kick of the match for dissent. Juve are seventh in the standings on 14 points, while Lecce are 12th. AC Milan eased past Udinese 2-0 in Sunday's late fixture, courtesy of an early goal from Christian Pulisic and a second-half strike by Omari Hutchinson. The victory in Udine lifts Milan to fourth place with 18 points while Udinese remain marooned in 17th after suffering their sixth consecutive league defeat. Earlier, Atalanta and Frosinone played out a 4–4 draw in Bergamo. Romano Schmid struck twice within the first 17 minutes for the visitors with home striker Nikola Krstovic also netting a brace.

item.title: Texans RB Woody Marks (leg) questionable to return
item.description: Houston Texans running back Woody Marks left Sunday's game with an apparent left knee injury when he was bent backward by New York Giants linebacker Micah McFadden.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Houston Texans running back Woody Marks left Sunday's game with an apparent left knee injury when he was bent backward by New York Giants linebacker Micah McFadden. Marks was hit below the knees and wrapped up by an oncoming McFadden. His left cleat was firmly planted as McFadden tried to finish the tackle, twisting Marks' left knee to the turf. Marks was ruled down by contact before the ball popped away for what, at first, was thought to be a fumble and defensive touchdown for the visiting Giants. Marks walked off the field under his own power and briefly went into the blue medical tent on the Texans' sideline. Dare Ogunbowale replaced Marks with Texans Week 1 starter David Montgomery inactive. Marks had 13 carries for 49 yards when he left the field. --Field Level Media

item.title: Reino Unido não integrará banco de defesa proposto por Canadá, diz fonte
item.description: O Reino Unido não aderirá ao Banco de Defesa, Segurança e Resiliência, liderado pelo Canadá, segundo uma fonte com conhecimento do assunto, mas os dois países afirmaram que irão desenvolver um mecanismo de cooperação entre suas respectivas iniciativas de financiamento para a defesa.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O Reino Unido não aderirá ao Banco de Defesa, Segurança e Resiliência, liderado pelo Canadá, segundo uma fonte com conhecimento do assunto, mas os dois países afirmaram que irão desenvolver um mecanismo de cooperação entre suas respectivas iniciativas de financiamento para a defesa. Em comunicado divulgado neste domingo, os dois governos disseram ter concordado em criar duas instituições distintas, mas complementares, para apoiar uma à outra em oportunidades de investimento e desafios estratégicos. "Temos trabalhado em estreita coordenação para avaliar como o Mecanismo Multilateral de Defesa (MDM, na sigla em inglês) e o Banco de Defesa, Segurança e Resiliência (DSRB, na sigla em inglês) podem melhor promover nossos objetivos comuns. Concordamos em desenvolver uma estrutura de cooperação que atenda aos interesses de ambas as instituições", diz o comunicado. Segundo outra fonte, os dois governos não conseguiram chegar a um acordo sobre questões-chave, incluindo a localização da sede do novo banco, o nível de compras conjuntas de equipamentos, a concessão de empréstimos aos países-membros e as regras para a admissão de novos integrantes no futuro. A fonte afirmou que o MDM terá como foco acelerar investimentos em defesa, financiar compras conjuntas e reunir a demanda dos aliados da Otan para reduzir custos de aquisição de equipamentos. Já o DSRB atuará de forma complementar, apoiando investimentos nas indústrias de defesa e nas cadeias de suprimentos, com maior foco em empréstimos soberanos individuais. O DSRB tem enfrentado dificuldades para obter apoio de grandes países europeus. O Reino Unido já havia se distanciado anteriormente do projeto. Reino Unido e Canadá afirmaram que o MDM e o DSRB serão estruturados para operar em estreita parceria, permitindo colaboração em prioridades industriais emergentes, oportunidades de investimento e desafios estratégicos de financiamento. (Reportagem de Anusha Shah em Bengaluru, Nivedita Balu em Toronto, William Schomberg e Elizabeth Piper em Londres)

item.title: Joe Marchant recalled to England squad for training camp
item.description: Centre Joe Marchant won a recall to the England squad on Sunday after being included in a 36-player training camp for next month's Nations Championship, the Rugby Football Union announced.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Centre Joe Marchant won a recall to the England squad on Sunday after being included in a 36-player training camp for next month's Nations Championship, the Rugby Football Union announced. Marchant left to play in France after the 2023 World Cup but, having returned to play for Sale Sharks, is eligible again and part of a three-day camp as coach Steve Borthwick decides on his final selections for home tests against Australia, Japan and New Zealand, all at Twickenham. Uncapped trio Greg Fisilau, Archie McParland and Kepu Tuipulotu are all called up, although they have been in previous squads or training camps. Captain Maro Itoje returns after an extended break, while Fin Baxter and Will Stuart are back after injury left them out of previous selections. Chandler Cunningham-South and Benhard Janse van Rensburg miss out through injury, while veteran lock Courtney Lawes, back in England after a stint in France, has not been recalled. Squad Backs: Noah Caluori (Saracens), Fraser Dingwall (Northampton), George Ford (Sale), Tommy Freeman (Northampton), George Furbank (Harlequins), Will Joseph (Gloucester), Joe Marchant (Sale), Archie McParland, Alex Mitchell (both Northampton), Cadan Murley (Harlequins), Max Ojomoh (Bath), Henry Slade (Exeter), Fin Smith (Northampton), Marcus Smith (Harlequins), Freddie Steward, Jack van Poortvliet (both Leicester) Forwards: Fin Baxter (Harlequins), Ollie Chessum (Leicester), Arthur Clark (Gloucester), Alex Coles (Northampton), Luke Cowan-Dickie, Ben Curry, Tom Curry (all Sale), Ben Earl (Saracens), Greg Fisilau (Exeter), Jamie George (Saracens), Ellis Genge (Bristol), Joe Heyes (Leicester), Maro Itoje (Saracens), Emmanuel Iyogun (Northampton), George Martin (Saracens), Asher Opoku-Fordjour (Sale), Tom Pearson, Henry Pollock (both Northampton), Will Stuart, Kepu Tuipulotu (both Bath).

item.title: Bayern Munich survive late scare to beat Freiburg 3-1
item.description: Bayern Munich preserved their unbeaten start to the Bundesliga season with a 3-1 victory at SC Freiburg, but the visitors were forced to withstand late pressure after Tom Bischof's own goal sparked a frantic push from the hosts for an equaliser.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bayern Munich preserved their unbeaten start to the Bundesliga season with a 3-1 victory at SC Freiburg, but the visitors were forced to withstand late pressure after Tom Bischof's own goal sparked a frantic push from the hosts for an equaliser. Bayern had been cruising at the Europa Park Stadion after taking an early lead when central defender Dayot Upamecano scored an unlikely opener in the 17th minute, sprinting forward through the middle on the counter-attack and latching on to a pass from Michael Olise before expertly slotting the ball past keeper Mio Backhaus. Freiburg, who got off to a superb start to the league season with four wins and a draw in their first five games before losing to Bayer Leverkusen, found themselves two down when winger Serge Gnabry surged down the left channel and finished from a tight angle three minutes before the break. The home side were thrown a lifeline when Bischof turned a pass from Rihito Yamamoto into his own net in the 82nd minute, but Olise restored his side's two-goal advantage deep into stoppage time to secure the win. Bayern are top of the table with 17 points from seven games, ahead of Borussia Dortmund on goal difference. Freiburg are third on 13 points. Earlier in the afternoon, Hoffenheim cruised to a 3-0 home win over Leverkusen but lost midfielder Alexander Prass to a late red card after he removed his shirt to celebrate scoring a goal. Facing the team fourth in the standings, Andrej Kramaric had given mid-table Hoffenheim the lead from the penalty spot in the 79th minute, and Prass all but wrapped up the three points for the home side by netting a second in the 89th minute. Forgetting that he had been booked on the stroke of half-time, Prass took off his shirt to celebrate and was horrified when he was shown a second yellow card before Max Moerstedt put the game beyond doubt with a third goal in the fifth minute of stoppage time.

item.title: Gol não cancelou “todos os voos” do Sul ao Nordeste; segundo Anac, aviação opera normalmente
item.description: A Gol não cancelou “todos os voos” saindo da região Sul para o Nordeste no último sábado, como afirmam publicações nas redes sociais. A companhia aérea cancelou apenas um voo, que ia de Porto Alegre para Salvador.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: A Gol não cancelou “todos os voos” saindo da região Sul para o Nordeste no último sábado, como afirmam publicações nas redes sociais. A companhia aérea cancelou apenas um voo, que ia de Porto Alegre para Salvador. “A companhia aérea Gol cancelou todos os voos de hoje, que iriam de parte do Sul do Brasil para o Nordeste”, dizem postagens no Instagram. A empresa informou em nota enviada à Reuters que o voo G31979, de Porto Alegre para Salvador marcado para o sábado, teve de ser cancelado por problemas técnicos com a aeronave. “Os clientes receberam as tratativas e foram reacomodados em outros voos da companhia”, afirmou. Segundo a assessoria da Gol, houve um voo extra após o ocorrido, e a aeronave pousou na capital baiana antes das 4h deste domingo. A Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil (Anac) declarou que “não há anormalidades no fluxo aéreo brasileiro” e que segue monitorando a movimentação. O órgão destacou que “atrasos e cancelamentos de voos fazem parte da rotina da aviação comercial”. De acordo com a agência, entre o sábado e este domingo de eleições, foram registrados outros três cancelamentos de voos para o Nordeste -- dois da Azul (um saindo de Brasília com destino a Recife, outro de Maceió também rumo à capital pernambucana) e um da Latam, de Guarulhos (SP) para Maceió.  A agência disse que entrou em contato com as três empresas para que informem as ações adotadas para realocar os passageiros.  O Ministério de Portos e Aeroportos também disse que está acompanhando a situação da aviação durante o pleito "para identificar prontamente eventuais problemas e assegurar a adoção das medidas necessárias para garantir o deslocamento dos eleitores". VEREDICTO Falso. A Gol cancelou somente um voo do Sul ao Nordeste neste fim de semana. Outras três viagens da Azul e da Latam para a região também foram suspensas. Segundo a Anac, a aviação brasileira está operando normalmente. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. Envie sugestões de checagem via WhatsApp pelo número (11) 91599-9278 . Leia mais sobre nosso trabalho de checagens de afirmações nas redes sociais aqui .

item.title: Report: Peyton Manning not expected to become Colts GM
item.description: Peyton Manning is not believed to be interested in the Indianapolis Colts' general manager job, and the team has not approached him about taking it, ESPN reported Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Peyton Manning is not believed to be interested in the Indianapolis Colts' general manager job, and the team has not approached him about taking it, ESPN reported Sunday. ESPN's sources said that the time commitment required to run an NFL front office would conflict with the Colts legend's post-playing projects -- Omaha Productions, the popular "Manningcast" with brother Eli as an alternative to ESPN/ABC's "Monday Night Football" telecasts, and his work as commercial spokesman. The Colts are looking for a new GM after firing Chris Ballard last week. Indianapolis began this season 2-4 after losing its final seven games in 2025. Ballard's teams were 72-82-1 during the regular season and 1-2 in the playoffs. The club last made the postseason in 2020. It did not win an AFC South division championships during Ballard's eight full seasons in charge. Manning said in 2024 that he was not focused on becoming a GM, but ESPN's sources noted that he is open to NFL opportunities, adding that they likely would need to be positions similar to the higher-level ones that former stars such as Tom Brady (Las Vegas Raiders part owner), Matt Ryan (Atlanta Falcons president of football operations) and Tony Boselli (Jacksonville Jaguars vice president of football operations) hold. Manning played 13 seasons for the Colts after being drafted No. 1 overall by Indianapolis in 1998. The Pro Football Hall of Famer threw for 54,828 yards and 399 touchdowns with the club. He was the QB when the Colts won Super Bowl XLI over the Chicago Bears in the 2006 season. After sitting out the 2011 season with shoulder and neck injuries, Manning was released by the Colts and signed with the Denver Broncos in 2012. He played four more seasons, retiring in 2015 after capturing a second Super Bowl ring that season, for Denver over the Carolina Panthers in Super Bowl 50. --Field Level Media

item.title: Britain will not join Canada's defence bank, source says
item.description: Britain will not join the Canada-led Defence Security and Resilience Bank, according to a source familiar with the matter, but the two countries said they would develop a framework for cooperation between their respective defence-funding initiatives.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain will not join the Canada-led Defence Security and Resilience Bank, according to a source familiar with the matter, but the two countries said they would develop a framework for cooperation between their respective defence-funding initiatives. In a statement on Sunday, the two governments said they had agreed to establish two distinct but complementary institutions to support each other on investment opportunities and strategic challenges. "We have been working closely to consider how the Multilateral Defence Mechanism (MDM) and Defence, Security and Resilience Bank (DSRB) can best advance our shared objectives. We have agreed to develop a framework of cooperation that works in the interest of both institutions," the statement said. According to another source, the two governments were unable to agree on key issues including the location of the headquarters of the new bank, the level of joint procurement, lending to members, and the rules around new members joining in the future. The source said the MDM will focus on accelerating defence investment, joint procurement through financing, and bringing together demand across NATO allies to reduce procurement costs, while the DSRB will complement it by supporting investment in defence industries and supply chains, focusing more on single sovereign lending. The DSRB has faced challenges securing support from larger European nations. Britain has previously distanced itself from the project. Britain and Canada said the MDM and DSRB will be designed to work in close partnership, so they can support each other on emerging industrial priorities, investment opportunities and strategic financing challenges.

item.title: Rennes go top of Ligue 1 with 3-0 win over Strasbourg
item.description: Rennes moved top of the Ligue 1 standings with a comprehensive 3-0 home triumph over RC Strasbourg on Sunday, moving one point ahead of Lille and AS Monaco, who drew earlier in the day.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Rennes moved top of the Ligue 1 standings with a comprehensive 3-0 home triumph over RC Strasbourg on Sunday, moving one point ahead of Lille and AS Monaco, who drew earlier in the day. Sebastian Szymanski scored a double for Rennes, who advanced to 16 points from eight games, with Boulaye Dia opening the scoring in a comfortable triumph. Lille and Monaco are level on 15 points after they played out a 1-1 draw in the Principality, with Ethan Mbappe opening the scoring in the 24th minute as Lille imposed their early dominance. New Monaco coach Filipe Luis switched things around with a bevy of changes for the second half and, following Tanguy Nianzou's dismissal in the 66th minute, Edan Diop equalised in the 74th minute. Champions Paris St Germain and Olympique Lyonnais are next in the standings with 14 points and will play in the capital on Monday. The clash at the Parc des Princes was moved from Sunday to Monday after police raised security concerns ahead of weekend protests that had hundreds of thousands of demonstrators marching on Saturday. Largely peaceful rallies gave way to clashes as night fell despite a huge security operation aimed at preventing a repeat of last week's unrest. Also on Sunday, there was a 4-3 home triumph for beleaguered Olympique de Marseille over Le Havre, helping them move up the league ladder after being stuck in the relegation zone just weeks ago. They are now eighth with 12 points, although it was a nerve-wracking affair for home fans before Marseille secured a third consecutive league victory. Le Havre had a penalty claim for possible handball seven minutes into stoppage time at the end of the game waved away after a VAR review. Marseille had led 4-0 in the 55th minute but nearly threw it away as Le Havre fought back to 4-3 with one minute to go. Le Havre remain bottom with two points from their first eight games of the season, three points adrift of Troyes, who picked up an away point in a goalless draw at Toulouse. There were also draws as Lorient were goalless away at Angers, while AJ Auxerre were held 1-1 at home by Le Mans.

item.title: Takeda to seek Japan approval for gastric cancer drug next year
item.description: Takeda Pharmaceutical plans to seek regulatory approval in Japan next year for its gastric cancer drug, after it extended overall survival and delayed disease progression in a late-stage study, a company executive told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Bhanvi Satija
item.content:encoded: Takeda Pharmaceutical (4502.T) plans to seek regulatory approval in Japan next year for its gastric cancer drug, after it extended overall survival and delayed disease progression in a late-stage study, a company executive told Reuters. The drug, arcotatug tavatecan, or TAK-921, met both those main goals of the trial in patients with advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer who had received at least two prior therapies. "We will leverage this data and file in Japan with an NDA next year," PK Morrow, who leads oncology development for the Japanese drugmaker, said in an interview on Saturday at the European Society for Medical Oncology meeting in Madrid, referring to a new drug application. Some analysts said the data was "a solid start" for Takeda's more focused strategy for its oncology ambitions. The company is prioritizing development in lung and chest cancers, blood cancers and gastric cancer. Median overall survival was 10.2 months for patients on the drug versus 6.9 months for those given doctor's choice of chemotherapy, a difference that was deemed statistically significant. Median progression-free survival, or the time it took for the disease to worsen, was 7.1 months for the Takeda drug versus 3.1 months in the control group, according to an independent review. For a majority of patients in the study, Takeda's drug was their third line of therapy, and for 30% of the patients it was a fourth or fifth treatment, Morrow said. "Despite the fact that patients were so sick, they were able to tolerate the therapy. And secondly, we were still able to show significant benefit," she said. About 47% of patients on the drug had serious side effects, compared with about 56% of those on chemotherapy. The most common was low red blood cell count, or anemia, which affected about 20% of patients on the drug versus about 13% on chemotherapy. The data from the study of 464 patients from Japan and China was presented on Friday at the ESMO meeting. Severe nausea, vomiting and diarrhea were also less frequent with the Takeda drug, but one patient on the drug died suddenly from an unknown cause that was linked to the treatment, the company said. Takeda's drug targets a protein found on the surface of certain cancer cells called claudin 18.2, which was used as a biomarker for selecting patients most likely to benefit. The medicine belongs to a class of therapy known as antibody-drug conjugates. It delivers the cancer-killing agent exatecan directly to tumor cells. Takeda's trial enrolled patients with at least 75% of tumor cells expressing the target protein, but Morrow said the drug could be tested in patients with lower levels, given its tolerability profile. A rival drug from AstraZeneca (AZN.L) , which targets the same protein, [USN:L4N4691TE TEXT:"met the overall survival goal"] in a global study but did not show benefit on progression-free survival. Takeda licensed its drug from partner Innovent (1801.HK) , which holds rights to the medication in China.

item.title: Roche afirma que divarasib redujo riesgo de muerte en 44% en ensayo clínico sobre cáncer de pulmón
item.description: La farmacéutica suiza Roche anunció el domingo que su fármaco experimental contra el cáncer de pulmón divarasib redujo el riesgo de muerte en un 44% en comparación con los tratamientos actuales, según un estudio de fase III.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La farmacéutica suiza Roche (ROPC.S) anunció el domingo que su fármaco experimental contra el cáncer de pulmón divarasib redujo el riesgo de muerte en un 44% en comparación con los tratamientos actuales, según un estudio de fase III. • Roche señaló que los pacientes con cáncer de pulmón no microcítico con mutación KRAS G12C que habían recibido tratamiento previo y a los que se les administró divarasib presentaron una supervivencia global media de casi 18 meses, frente a los 12 meses de aquellos tratados con sotorasib o adagrasib • El divarasib también redujo el riesgo de progresión de la enfermedad o de muerte en un 42%, con una supervivencia media sin progresión de 9,8 meses frente a los 5,7 meses del grupo de control • El ensayo de fase III Krascendo 1 contó con la participación de 338 pacientes y comparó el divarasib con los dos inhibidores de KRAS G12C ya autorizados • La tasa de respuesta objetiva fue del 58% con divarasib, frente al 32% con sotorasib o adagrasib • No se observaron nuevos hallazgos en materia de seguridad. Alrededor del 4,8% de los pacientes tratados con divarasib interrumpieron el tratamiento debido a acontecimientos adversos relacionados con el mismo, frente al 11,7% del grupo de control • Los resultados se presentaron en el Congreso de la Sociedad Europea de Oncología Médica y se publicaron en la revista New England Journal of Medicine

item.title: Marine Le Pen anuncia candidatura a la presidencia de Francia mientras protestas sacuden el país
item.description: La líder de extrema derecha Marine Le Pen, favorita para las elecciones presidenciales francesas del año que viene, lanzó oficialmente su campaña el domingo con la promesa de restablecer el orden y la confianza nacional.
item.dc:creator: Lafken Zepeda, Nicolas Economou
item.content:encoded: La líder de extrema derecha Marine Le Pen, favorita para las elecciones presidenciales francesas del año que viene, lanzó oficialmente su campaña el domingo con la promesa de restablecer el orden y la confianza nacional. Mientras Francia se enfrenta a uno de sus períodos más turbulentos de los últimos años, Le Pen se presentó como la mejor opción para capear lo que describió como crecientes crisis económicas, sociales y de seguridad. "No estamos viviendo el fin del mundo, sino el fin de un mundo, su mundo", afirmó refiriéndose a sus oponentes políticos. Le Pen eligió pronunciar su primer discurso de campaña en Orleans, cuna de Juana de Arco, la heroína del siglo XV venerada por los nacionalistas como símbolo de patriotismo y soberanía. Dirigiéndose a una multitud de seguidores que la aclamaban, prometió una política de "tolerancia cero" y afirmó que restablecer la seguridad era el primer deber del Estado. Las protestas masivas por el costo de vida y la desigualdad del pasado fin de semana degeneraron en saqueos y actos de vandalismo. Los disturbios callejeros han dado un impulso a Le Pen y una encuesta de opinión publicada el domingo la sitúa entre el 32% y el 33,5% de las preferencias, muy por delante de su rival más cercano, el líder de la extrema izquierda Jean-Luc Mélenchon, con un 17%, a medida que los votantes abandonan los partidos mayoritarios para decantarse por los extremos políticos. Las encuestas sugieren que derrotaría fácilmente a Mélenchon en una segunda vuelta, que se prevé que se celebre a principios de mayo. En un intento por transmitir optimismo, Le Pen centró su discurso en el tema de un "renacimiento" nacional. Afirmó que Francia atraviesa un período de agitación, pero que saldría fortalecida si adoptara su visión de seguridad, prosperidad y renovación. Le Pen prometió mano dura en materia de inmigración, comprometiéndose a restablecer los controles fronterizos, expulsar automáticamente a los delincuentes extranjeros y tomar medidas enérgicas contra las bandas y los traficantes de drogas. La propia Le Pen podría verse obligada a hacer campaña con una tobillera electrónica tras haber sido condenada por malversación de fondos del Parlamento Europeo. Ha recurrido la sentencia judicial. En materia económica, Le Pen se comprometió a aplicar medidas de austeridad, reducir los impuestos a las empresas, recortar la burocracia y apoyar a la industria, la innovación y la inteligencia artificial. Rechazó nuevos aumentos de la edad de jubilación.

item.title: UK's Burnham says he is open to discussing EU free movement
item.description: Official data has shown long-term net migration in 2025 fell to close to its level before a new post-Brexit immigration system was introduced at the start of 2021.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

UK's Burnham says he is open to discussing EU free movement

Official data has shown long-term net migration in 2025 fell to close to its level before a new post-Brexit immigration system was introduced at the start of 2021.

Britain's Prime Minister Andy Burnham speaks as he delivers a speech during the The Innovation Nation Summit at Bruntwood SciTech on Oct 9, 2026, in Manchester. (File photo: Pool via Reuters/Christopher Furlong)

FAST

LONDON: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said he wants a discussion about returning to the European Union's freedom of movement rules for workers, a key issue in the 2016 Brexit referendum which led to Britain leaving the bloc. Building on previous comments about the need to rethink ties with Brussels, Burnham told the Sunday Times that the influx of EU workers into Britain before Brexit had posed very significant challenges. "But, at the same time, it was a type of immigration that perhaps wasn't as difficult (as now)," he said. "Revolving door migration where people would come and then go back is different. The balance of migration has changed, hasn't it, since then? I think we’ve just got to have an honest discussion about those things." Official data has shown long-term net migration in 2025 fell to close to its level before a new post-Brexit immigration system was introduced at the start of 2021.

In September, two months after replacing Keir Starmer as Labour Party leader and prime minister, Burnham said Britain should consider options for its relationship with the EU, including possibly rejoining the bloc one day. He had previously backed the pledges of Starmer's government which included no return to freedom of movement which Brussels sets as a condition for being part of the bloc's single market. In his interview with the Sunday Times, conducted on Oct 19, Burnham said the issue of freedom of movement could be considered as part of a broader reset of Britain's relationship with the EU, including on data sharing and migration.

Related:

Burnham hopes for EU deal next month, stirs Brexit debate

'Welcome back,' says Macron, as UK PM opens door to EU return

"You've got to see it in the round, rather than just looking at freedom of movement on its own," he said. Burnham, who is trying to find ways to speed up Britain's economy, is due to meet top EU officials for a summit on Nov 20. He said he could not imagine recommending that Britain adopt the euro currency or the EU's border-free travel arrangements. A new referendum would be needed to rejoin the EU but not necessarily to join the bloc's single market or a customs union, the Sunday Times quoted Burnham as saying. Former Conservative finance minister Jeremy Hunt, who campaigned to stay in the EU in 2016, said it would be a mistake to reopen one of the fundamental debates of the referendum and he said relaxing immigration rules would hurt people in Britain. "I think it will be a hammer blow to getting people off welfare and into work," Hunt told Sky News.

Source: Reuters/fs
