item.title: Les Brésiliens aux urnes pour un second tour serré entre Lula et Bolsonaro
item.description: Les Brésiliens votaient dimanche pour un second tour de la présidentielle qui s'annonce serré et qui pourrait faire basculer le plus grand pays d'Amérique latine vers la droite, comme nombre de pays de la région.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Griffin, Luciana Novaes Magalhaes, Marta Nogueira
item.content:encoded: Les Brésiliens votaient dimanche pour un second tour de la présidentielle qui s'annonce serré et qui pourrait faire basculer le plus grand pays d'Amérique latine vers la droite, comme nombre de pays de la région. Le sénateur Flavio Bolsonaro, fils de l'ancien président Jair Bolsonaro, actuellement emprisonné, part légèrement favori face au chef de l'Etat sortant Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, après avoir créé la surprise au début du mois en arrivant en tête au premier tour avec 47% des voix, contre 45% à Lula. Un juge de la Cour suprême a décidé de prolonger de deux heures les opérations de vote, qui devaient se terminer à 17h00 (20h00 GMT), en raison de problèmes de transports publics dénoncés par l'équipe de campagne de Lula. Une victoire de Flavio Bolsonaro, 45 ans, prolongerait la série de victoires enregistrées dans les urnes par des candidats de droite latino-américains revendiquant une proximité avec le président des États-Unis, Donald Trump. A l'inverse, un quatrième mandat de Lula ne serait pas vu d'un bon oeil par Washington, qui s'est heurté au président de gauche sur les questions commerciales et de sécurité. Samedi, Reuters a révélé l'existence d'une campagne menée par le département d'État américain pour aider les Bolsonaro à revenir au pouvoir. La campagne électorale a été marquée par des scandales de corruption et des accusations d'ingérence américaine, malgré les dénégations de Washington, avec en toile de fond la condamnation de Jair Bolsonaro en 2025 pour avoir fomenté un coup d'État après sa défaite à la présidentielle trois ans plus tôt, son fils s'étant engagé à le faire sortir de prison s'il est élu. Donald Trump a qualifié la condamnation de Jair Bolsonaro de "chasse aux sorcières" et a imposé en représailles des droits de douane de 50% au Brésil. Bien que cette mesure ait ensuite été assouplie, les États-Unis ont imposé cette année de nouvelles sanctions au Brésil, invoquant des pratiques commerciales déloyales. ACCUSATIONS D'INGÉRENCE AMÉRICAINE Lula a accusé l'administration Trump d'ingérence électorale et dénoncé des actes d'intimidation de la part de Washington. "On ne peut pas leur livrer le Brésil", a approuvé Elenildes dos Reis, une avocate de 60 ans, après avoir voté dimanche pour Lula à São Paulo. "Ce ne sera pas seulement notre victoire, ce sera celle du monde entier", a-t-elle ajouté. Sur le plan économique, malgré la baisse des inégalités et du chômage, Lula a eu du mal à convaincre un électorat confronté à la hausse du coût de la vie et de l'endettement des ménages. Flavio Bolsonaro a promis de lutter contre la vie chère et d'adopter des méthodes musclées contre la violence des gangs qui a aussi pesé dans la campagne. "Nous avons besoin de changement", a déclaré José Carlos Jarra, un retraité de 61 ans qui a voté pour le candidat Flavio Bolsonaro à São Paulo. À Rio de Janeiro, Alba Marques, une retraitée de 75 ans, a dit avoir voté pour Flavio Bolsonaro pour sanctionner le Parti des travailleurs de Lula, et non par adhésion au programme du candidat d'extrême droite. "Je ne supporte plus qu'un type passe 40 ans à dire qu'il va redresser le Brésil. Toujours la même promesse", a-t-elle dit à propos du président octogénaire. Les derniers sondages d'intention de vote plaçaient les deux candidats au coude-à-coude à la veille du scrutin, la principale incertitude venant de la mobilisation des abstentionnistes. Aucun candidat arrivé en tête au premier tour n'a jamais perdu au second tour de la présidentielle au Brésil.

item.title: Paris game played in festive atmosphere after fresh demonstrations
item.description: Protests largely overshadowed the build-up to the first NFL regular-season game.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Daheron
item.content:encoded: The Pittsburgh Steelers defeated the New Orleans Saints 16-10 in the first NFL regular-season game in Paris on Sunday, in a calm and festive atmosphere, a day after fresh demonstrations drew more than 100,000 people into the French capital. The nationwide protests largely overshadowed the build-up to the game, with some fan and NFL [USN:L6N46912R TEXT:"events cancelled"] over the weekend, mainly due to their location in central Paris. On Sunday, as Saturday’s rain gave way to sunshine, the mood was peaceful before kickoff around the Stade de France in Saint-Denis, some 10km (6 miles) north of Paris centre and more than 13km (8 miles) from Porte d'Italie, where Saturday's protests began in southern Paris. James Brown, a 51-year-old Saints fan who travelled to Paris especially for the game, told Reuters the atmosphere around the stadium was "wonderful, really good". The police presence appeared neither heavy nor unusual at the Stade de France, which hosted rugby sevens and athletics during the 2024 Paris Olympics and regularly serves as the home ground for the French national rugby and soccer teams. Hundreds of thousands of demonstrators marched in France on Saturday, with largely peaceful rallies giving way to clashes in Paris and Marseille as night fell despite a huge security operation aimed at preventing a repeat of last week's unrest. The main demonstration took place on the southeastern fringes of Paris, where at least 110,000 people turned out to denounce rising living costs and growing inequality. "We didn't notice much yesterday," 38-year-old Steelers fan Lukas Baldridge told Reuters. "We came in, went to a bar, got some drinks, got dinner, went home, didn't see any protesting. "Streets were closed. Most shops were closed. That felt unusual maybe but I don't know enough about Paris to know what is normal and what's not normal." The party was in full swing in a packed stadium when the game kicked off at 2.30 p.m. (1330 GMT), after French stars Antoine Dupont and Teddy Riner were introduced to the crowd. A couple of hours earlier, some Steelers players had arrived at the Stade de France dressed like characters from Peaky Blinders. Steelers fans seemed to outnumber their opponents, even though the neutral-site game was officially hosted by the Saints. "It kind of felt 50/50," Saints linebacker Kaden Elliss told a press conference. "This is such a fun atmosphere. Maybe not feel like the true home team, it was a very special atmosphere, one I wish we could have gotten a win in." Nigerian rapper Burna Boy and French singer Yseult performed during a brief halftime show. "I would like to start by saying how much we appreciate everyone who, in the country of France, Paris, Versailles, helped make this event happen," Saints coach Kellen Moore told a press conference. "I thought it was a really great event, really great game today."

item.title: What are Brazilian voters' main concerns?
item.description: Brazilians headed to the ballot box on Sunday, in a runoff vote that pits right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, against leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.
item.dc:creator: Isabel Teles
item.content:encoded: Brazilians headed to the ballot box on Sunday, in a runoff vote that pits right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, against leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. Here are the main themes that have driven the campaign: INFLATION Cost-of-living concerns are widespread. More than two-thirds of respondents told a Quaest poll in August their purchasing power [USN:L6N459162 TEXT:"had declined"] versus the previous year. Annual inflation stood at 4.58% in the 12 months through September, above the central bank's 3% target, pushing prices — including for food — higher Lula has pledged to implement measures to allow for steady cuts in borrowing costs and keep inflation under control Bolsonaro wants to reduce and stabilize public debt to bring interest rates closer to international levels and steer inflation toward the central bank's target CRIME Crime is another major [USN:L1N45Z0NR TEXT:"concern"] for Brazilians. While Brazil's homicide rate fell by 40% over the last decade, improvements in fighting crime have been uneven, according to the Brazilian Public Security Forum, a think tank. Bolsonaro has pledged a heavy-handed approach to criminals, promising maximum-security prisons and chemical castration for serious sexual offenses Lula wants to increase the federal prison system's capacity to hold gang leaders, while still investing in poor areas to reduce the influence of organized crime CORRUPTION Corruption is also at the top of voters' minds, with both Lula's circle and Bolsonaro [USN:L6N46611M TEXT:"facing scrutiny"] in high-profile cases. A major scandal that led to the collapse of mid-size lender Banco Master has sparked multiple probes, including into [USN:L6N3ZZ1EP TEXT:"Bolsonaro"] over alleged corruption and money laundering, accusations he denies Bolsonaro has pledged to fight corruption by shielding state-run companies and pension funds from political appointments and expanding transparency in public spending Lula has vowed to deepen anti-corruption and transparency policies even as his son - who has denied the allegations - is being investigated in probes involving alleged influence peddling, corruption and fraud PUBLIC FINANCES Brazil's public finances are under pressure, especially due to pensions and social benefits. The difficult fiscal outlook has sparked fears of welfare cuts, while many Brazilians are struggling with debt arrears due to years of double-digit interest rates. Public debt has risen by more than 10 percentage points during Lula's current term, reaching [USN:L1N45M0ES TEXT:"82.9%"] of gross domestic product Brazil's benchmark interest rate of [USN:L6N458186 TEXT:"13.75%"] remains among the highest in the world Long-term interest rates [USN:L1N45R06Y TEXT:"fell sharply"] after Bolsonaro's stronger-than-expected first-round performance He has promised to ramp up [USN:L1N4580UE TEXT:"fiscal adjustment"], targeting 1.5% of GDP improvement in the primary balance within 18 months to lower borrowing costs Lula has reiterated commitments to improve Brazil's primary balance targeting an [USN:L1N44S10B TEXT:"effective surplus"] near 1.3% of GDP by 2030, versus a projected 0.4% deficit this year FOREIGN POLICY After US President Donald Trump imposed [USN:L6N3TR0ZD TEXT:"tariffs"] on a swathe of Brazilian goods in 2025, foreign policy became a more prominent issue for many Brazilians. Bolsonaro has courted Trump and other right-wing allies globally He wants to rebuild ties with Argentina, the US and Israel, arguing relations with each are close to breaking point Lula has campaigned for a foreign policy based on multilateralism and stronger ties with the Mercosur bloc of South American states and the BRICS nations ($1 = 5.0086 reais)

item.title: French protest groups demand more rallies as Macron faces tough choices
item.description: The government began talks with unions and student representatives to defuse the crisis, but protest leaders say the measures it has proposed are inadequate.
item.dc:creator: Crispian Balmer, Juliette Jabkhiro
item.content:encoded: French protest groups and unions called on Sunday for further demonstrations as they sought to maintain pressure on the government after a huge security operation helped to contain unrest during nationwide rallies on Saturday. The Interior Ministry said 410,000 people took part in Saturday's marches as authorities deployed 70,000 police, helping to avert a repeat of the looting and vandalism that swept many cities on October 17. Labour leaders urged further protests next Saturday and a nationwide strike on November 5, saying frustration over wages, living costs and public services was spreading far beyond the student movement that first mobilised last month. "We see an aggregation of anger," Murielle Guilbert, co-leader of the left-wing Solidaires trade union federation, told BFM TV. She said grievances from students, workers, firefighters and other groups were converging. "We call on people to take to the streets next Saturday." The SUD Education teaching union said it would join the October 31 demonstration while the large CGT union said it would decide during the week. MACRON'S SCOPE TO RESPOND IS MINIMAL The Yellow Vests, a grassroots movement that emerged in 2018 as a revolt against fuel taxes, also called for mass rallies next Saturday, including sit-ins outside town halls and the National Assembly. "There is anger in this country. It's growing in schools and universities, on roundabouts, in neighbourhoods, on farms and in workplaces," activist Azelma Sigaux told reporters. In 2019, President Emmanuel Macron was able to find the resources to reduce fuel costs in response to the Yellow Vests. Seven years on, strained public finances leave him with little room to meet protesters' demands. His mandate also expires next April and his centrist party no longer has the majority needed to pass major legislation. The government has begun talks with unions and student representatives to try to defuse the crisis, but protest leaders say the measures it has proposed so far are inadequate. "We have received no response at all from this government," said Guilbert. Police unions said on Sunday they did not have enough staff to maintain for any length of time the high level of deployment that on Saturday helped to limit disorder to sporadic clashes in a number of cities, including Paris and Marseille. Some 1,314 people were arrested on Saturday, half of last week's numbers, the interior ministry said on Sunday, and about 50 police were injured, compared with more than 1,000 last week. The protests have resonated beyond France's borders. On Saturday [USN:L6N46A05C TEXT:"Belgian police"] used tear gas and pepper spray as they clashed in Brussels with anti-government demonstrators. [USN:FWN4630JL TEXT:"In Albania"], peaceful protests that began at the end of May this month turned into violent unrest and skirmishes have taken place in several Italian cities for a second week running.

item.title: Brasil extiende votación en reñido balotaje presidencial entre Lula y Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Los brasileños votaban el domingo en una reñida segunda vuelta electoral que podría inclinar bruscamente a la derecha a la nación más grande de América Latina, acercándola a Estados Unidos como parte de un giro conservador más amplio en toda la región.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Griffin
item.content:encoded: Los brasileños votaban el domingo en una reñida segunda vuelta electoral que podría inclinar bruscamente a la derecha a la nación más grande de América Latina, acercándola a Estados Unidos como parte de un giro conservador más amplio en toda la región. El balotaje enfrenta al presidente izquierdista Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva con el senador derechista Flávio Bolsonaro. El hijo del expresidente Jair Bolsonaro dio la sorpresa a principios de mes al liderar la votación en la primera vuelta en contra de lo que decían las encuestas. El magistrado del Supremo Tribunal Federal Cristiano Zanin ordenó que se ampliara en dos horas el horario de votación, accediendo a una solicitud de la campaña de Lula. En un principio, estaba previsto que las urnas cerraran a las 17:00 hora de Brasilia (2000 GMT). La campaña de Lula denunció que las autoridades de varias ciudades estaban restringiendo el acceso de los votantes al transporte público. En tanto, la autoridad electoral del país anunció que pausaba el recuento de los sufragios hasta que se cumpla el horario ampliado de la votación. Bolsonaro solicitó tiempo adicional en tres estados, alegando mal clima, mientras que Lula pidió que ampliaran el horario de votación en nueve estados después de que su campaña denunciara que las autoridades habían reducido el servicio de transporte público el día de las elecciones. Muchos brasileños dependen del transporte público para votar en las ciudades en las que están empadronados, pero en las que quizá no residan. Los seguidores de Lula suelen depender en mayor medida del transporte público en estas ciudades. Un tribunal del estado de Bahía, bastión de Lula en el noreste, ordenó la detención de un alto cargo del transporte en Salvador por las acusaciones de que ordenó una reducción de la flota de autobuses de la ciudad. "Nadie debería renunciar a votar porque algún empresario sin escrúpulos o algún alcalde corrupto y deshonesto haya intentado impedírselo", declaró Lula a periodistas. Un triunfo de Bolsonaro, de 45 años, prolongaría la ola de victorias de la derecha para los candidatos latinoamericanos afines a Donald Trump, mientras que un cuarto mandato para Lula sería una decepción en Washington, que ha tenido roces con su gobierno en materia de comercio y seguridad. Reuters reveló el sábado una campaña dentro del Departamento de Estado de Trump para ayudar a que los Bolsonaro volvieran al poder. La contienda electoral ha estado marcada por escándalos de corrupción, incertidumbre económica y acusaciones de injerencia estadounidense, algo que Washington niega. También se ha visto influenciada por las repercusiones de la condena de Jair Bolsonaro en 2025 por planear un golpe de Estado en 2022, ante la promesa de Flávio de liberar a su padre si resulta elegido. Trump calificó el caso de "caza de brujas" e impuso un arancel del 50% a Brasil en 2025, en una decisión vinculada explícitamente al juicio de Jair Bolsonaro. Si bien muchas de estas medidas fueron posteriormente suavizadas, el mandatario republicano impuso nuevos aranceles a Brasil este año, alegando prácticas comerciales desleales. Lula ha presentado la cercanía del Gobierno de Trump con el clan Bolsonaro como parte de un intento de influir en las elecciones, al tiempo que ha calificado los aranceles y otras medidas punitivas de intimidación. "No podemos entregar Brasil", afirmó Elenildes dos Reis, una abogada de 60 años de São Paulo que votó por Lula y señaló que su victoria sería una forma de plantarle cara a Trump y a lo que ella describió como una ola creciente de fascismo. "No será solo nuestra victoria, será la del mundo", añadió. En materia económica, a pesar de la disminución de la desigualdad y el desempleo, Lula ha tenido dificultades para ganarse a un electorado que lidia con el alto costo de la vida y las elevadas deudas familiares. La violencia endémica de las pandillas también preocupa a los votantes. RESULTADO INCIERTO Bolsonaro ha intentado sacar provecho de la preocupación por el costo de la vida y también ha prometido mano dura para combatir la delincuencia, comprometiéndose a construir cárceles de máxima seguridad y a aplicar la castración química para los delitos sexuales graves. "Necesitamos un cambio", afirmó José Carlos Jarra, un jubilado de 61 años de São Paulo que trabajó en el sector sanitario y votó a Bolsonaro. Dijo esperar que el senador abordara la seguridad pública y hiciera más por los jubilados, y calificó el salario mínimo de Brasil como "una vergüenza". En Río de Janeiro, Alba Marques, una jubilada de 75 años, afirmó que su voto por Bolsonaro era un voto en contra del Partido de los Trabajadores de Lula, no a favor del senador. "Ya no soporto que, desde hace 40 años, un tipo diga que va a arreglar Brasil. Siempre la misma promesa", afirmó. Al emitir su voto en Río de Janeiro el domingo, Flávio Bolsonaro instó a la gente a acudir a las urnas "con lluvia o con sol". Lula, por su parte, votará en São Bernardo do Campo, cerca de São Paulo. Las encuestas muestran que los candidatos están prácticamente empatados de cara a la segunda vuelta, con recortando distancias en los últimos días. Lula votó en São Bernardo do Campo, cerca de São Paulo, y agradeció a sus seguidores. "Lo que la gente ha hecho por mí estos últimos días es algo que nunca podré devolver", dijo a periodistas. Los precedentes históricos favorecen a Bolsonaro, ya que ningún candidato ha ganado la presidencia tras quedar segundo en la primera vuelta de las elecciones. Bolsonaro obtuvo el 47% de los votos emitidos en la primera vuelta, contra e 45% de Lula. La victoria del senador disparó los mercados brasileños y su moneda ante las expectativas de reformas favorables a las empresas. Su éxito en la primera vuelta se vio reflejado en las elecciones al Congreso de su Partido Liberal y de otros políticos de derecha, lo que podría allanarle el camino legislativo o complicarle la gobernabilidad a Lula.

item.title: Disputa acirrada entre Flávio e Lula pode ser definida pela abstenção; cidades enfrentam problemas no transporte
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) decidem neste domingo quem governará o Brasil a partir de 5 de janeiro de 2027 após uma das campanhas eleitorais mais tensas e recheadas de acusações da história da política brasileira, sem que as pesquisas apontem um favorito claro e com um provável papel decisivo do comparecimento dos eleitores às urnas.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Simões
item.content:encoded: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) decidem neste domingo quem governará o Brasil a partir de 5 de janeiro de 2027 após uma das campanhas eleitorais mais tensas e recheadas de acusações da história da política brasileira, sem que as pesquisas apontem um favorito claro e com um provável papel decisivo do comparecimento dos eleitores às urnas. Neste cenário, algumas cidades do país enfrentavam problemas no transporte público, e a Justiça eleitoral determinou a [USN:L2N46B04J TEXT:"prisão"] de um secretário municipal de Salvador sob acusação de restrição de transporte público. Flávio Bolsonaro, senador de 45 anos e filho mais velho do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, largou na frente na disputa pelo Planalto após um resultado surpreendente no primeiro turno, disputado há três semanas, quando terminou na liderança com 47,03% dos votos, contra 45,16% de Lula. O atual presidente e candidato à reeleição, que completará 81 anos na próxima terça-feira e que busca um quarto mandato presidencial, reduziu gradativamente a distância para o rival nas pesquisas de intenção de voto mais recentes, o que leva a corrida a um cenário incerto. “O que o povo fez comigo nesses dias é uma coisa que não tem como pagar, é muita generosidade, é muito carinho, é muito amor e eu serei eternamente grato ao comportamento do povo”, disse o petista a jornalistas após votar na manhã deste domingo, em São Bernardo do Campo (SP), berço político do Partido dos Trabalhadores. As [USN:L2N46A047 TEXT:"pesquisas divulgadas na véspera"] da votação deste domingo mostraram um empate técnico com vantagem numérica de Flávio sobre Lula de no máximo dois pontos percentuais nos votos válidos, com 51% a 49%. "Flávio é ligeiramente favorito, ele não é francamente favorito", disse o cientista político Carlos Melo, do Insper. "Quando você olha para as pesquisas, mais do que o número você tem que olhar para a tendência. A tendência é o Flávio caindo, ou praticamente paralisado, e o Lula subindo muito devagar", acrescentou, apontando que não é possível prever se essa tendência resultará em uma virada a favor de Lula neste domingo. Um dos fatores cruciais a ser observado, na avaliação de Melo, será o comparecimento às urnas, já que historicamente o eleitorado que tende a apoiar mais Lula e o PT costuma ter um comparecimento menor. Não à toa, a campanha de Lula vem concentrando esforços em incentivar pessoas que não votaram no primeiro turno a comparecerem na seção eleitoral neste domingo. No primeiro turno, mais de 33,4 milhões de eleitores não foram votar, uma abstenção de 21,08%, em um total de mais de 158,7 milhões de eleitores aptos a votar. Neste domingo, Flávio Bolsonaro também fez um apelo para que os eleitores compareçam às urnas. "Faça chuva ou faça sol, bora sair de casa para votar, que o Brasil vai mudar e o Brasil vai vencer", disse o senador, após votar no Rio de Janeiro, repetindo apelo já feito em suas redes sociais na véspera, em meio à previsão de chuvas fortes nas regiões Sul e Sudeste, onde teve desempenho melhor que Lula. "Chegou a hora da mudança de verdade", afirmou o candidato, ao lado da esposa Fernanda e da mãe, Rogéria. ÔNIBUS Em uma campanha marcada por grande movimentação das duas campanhas contra os adversários no Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), que levou o presidente da corte Kassio Nunes Marques a pedir que as campanhas moderassem a quantidade de ações, há receios de que, independentemente do vencedor, ocorram novos embates mesmo após a declaração do resultado. A expectativa de uma margem apertada a favor do eleito também leva a crer que isso possa ocorrer. "A expectativa é de que vai ser uma eleição tensa", disse Creomar de Souza, analista político da Dharma Political Risk. "Acho que a gente ainda vai ter algum nível de discussão política, algum nível de embate jurídico", avaliou. Em meio a essas expectativas, Tribunais Regionais Eleitorais tiveram que agir para sanar problemas no transporte público. O presidente do TRE da Bahia, Mauricio Szporer, [USN:L2N46B04J TEXT:"determinou"] no início da tarde deste domingo a prisão do secretário municipal de Mobilidade de Salvador (Semob), Pablo Souza, sob acusação de ter orientado a redução da frota de ônibus na cidade no dia do segundo turno das eleições. Lula teve mais de 65% dos votos válidos no primeiro turno em Salvador, cujo prefeito, Bruno Reis, é do União Brasil. Em São Paulo, o TRE atendeu a um pedido do PSOL e determinou que a prefeitura colocasse 100% da frota de ônibus para circular neste domingo, com multa de R$100 mil ao prefeito e ao presidente da SPTrans em caso de descumprimento. Em declaração a jornalistas, Lula disse que não aceitaria essa situação. "Não vamos aceitar banditismo e mau-caratismo nem de prefeito, nem de governador", disse o presidente. Ele aproveitou para fazer um apelo que os eleitores não deixem de votar: "Não desistam de votar, esperem e votem". Em entrevista à imprensa, Nunes Marques afirmou que há demanda no TSE para prolongar o período de votação do segundo turno e, sem dar detalhes, disse que "isso certamente, como toda e qualquer ação, será analisado a seu tempo". "De fato, em alguns locais há uma dificuldade ainda no transporte, já está sendo corrigida", disse. Ele acrescentou que o TSE está recebendo, periodicamente, relatórios do TRE da Bahia. DEMOCRACIA E MUDANÇA Eleitores relatavam uma votação sem as filas vistas no primeiro turno, quando foi preciso votar também para deputado federal e estadual, senadores e governador. Neste segundo turno, apenas cinco Estados e o Distrito Federal têm votação para governador, além da eleição para presidente. A bibliotecária aposentada Hilda Corrêa, de 80 anos, fez questão de votar em Brasília, mesmo com o voto não sendo obrigatório a partir dos 70 anos. "Eu exerço essa cidadania minha desde que eu comecei a votar. E eu passei um tempo em que a gente não votava, quando eu era mais jovem, por causa da ditadura... Agora, tem que votar todo tempo. Pela democracia", disse ela, que anunciou voto em Lula. "Ele vai ser muito melhor do que essa turma da bala que está aí." Já o também aposentado José Carlos Jarra, de 61 anos, votou em Flávio Bolsonaro em São Paulo. "A gente precisa da mudança. Eu gostaria que ele (Flávio) mudasse a segurança, olhasse mais pelos aposentados, pelo salário mínimo, que aqui no Brasil é uma vergonha. Também rezo para que o Flávio e o Senado mexam neste Supremo Tribunal Federal", afirmou ele. CAMPANHA ENGRENA As três semanas de campanha do segundo turno foram bastante diferentes dos meses que antecederam o primeiro turno, realizado no dia 4 de outubro. No caso de Lula, uma guinada em direção a uma mobilização maciça nas redes sociais e em eventos de rua. Na véspera da votação, antes de participar de evento de campanha em Copacabana, Lula afirmou que "o povo assumiu para si a responsabilidade de fazer a campanha". Um dos destaques da campanha petista no segundo turno foi o impulso nas redes, liderado pelo canal de WhatsApp "Exército do Lula", criado pelo deputado federal reeleito André Janones (Rede-MG), que juntou mais de 10 milhões de pessoas para ouvir as "missões" que Janones dava para os apoiadores cumprirem nas redes. A campanha de Flávio chegou a entrar no TSE pedindo a suspensão do canal. A guinada digital da campanha petista teve como ápice Lula -- crítico público do uso frequente de celular que se orgulhava de não ter o aparelho -- ganhando um de presente do governador reeleito do Piauí, Rafael Fonteles (PT), e passando a fazer vários vídeos no formato selfie para apoiadores. Neste quadro, a Meta (META.O) -- proprietária do Facebook, do Instagram e do WhatsApp -- também ficou no foco, após a campanha de Lula apontar que teve sua atuação restrita nas plataformas da empresa, levando a big tech norte-americana a prestar esclarecimentos ao TSE. Do lado de Flávio, após a inesperada liderança no dia 4, o senador deu declarações que geraram polêmica, como quando disse que, se eleito, usará a força que terá no próximo Congresso para alterar a Constituição. Posteriormente, afirmou que iria propor mudanças constitucionais como o fim da reeleição e a redução da maioridade penal. Também acabou mudando de posição em temas pautados por Lula, como o fim da escala de trabalho 6x1, para o qual ele votou favoravelmente no Senado, apesar de, num passado muito recente, ter se declarado contrário. O senador, por outro lado, também conseguiu mobilizar grandes públicos em atos de campanha em todo o país, no que foi uma marca da campanha de ambos os lados. Uma vitória de Flávio Bolsonaro ampliaria uma onda de triunfos de candidatos de direita na América Latina alinhados ao presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, enquanto um quarto mandato de Lula seria uma decepção para Washington, que teve atritos com o governo do petista em questões de comércio e segurança. Até o momento, Trump evitou declarar apoio a qualquer candidato. Questionado no domingo sobre quem ele gostaria que vencesse, Trump não quis responder. "Não quero entrar nesse assunto, mas estamos acompanhando", disse ele a jornalistas em Washington.

item.title: Uganda imposes 21-day quarantine on citizens returning from Congo
item.description: Ugandan citizens returning to the country with a history of travel to Democratic Republic of Congo will be quarantined for 21 days, Health Minister Chris Baryomunsi said on Sunday as Uganda tightened Ebola precautions.
item.dc:creator: Elias Biryabarema
item.content:encoded: Ugandan citizens returning to the country with a history of travel to Democratic Republic of Congo will be quarantined for 21 days, Health Minister Chris Baryomunsi said on Sunday as Uganda tightened Ebola precautions. Uganda says it is Ebola-free after [USN:S8N41P031 TEXT:"declaring an end"] to its latest outbreak in July, but there has been concern among health experts after two people who had recently passed through the country later tested positive in [USN:SPN45F00J TEXT:"Kenya"] and [USN:L8N4682IW TEXT:"Nigeria"]. Uganda says it is investigating the Nigerian case, which involves the wife of a Swiss diplomat. The woman, 42, returned from Uganda through Addis Ababa to Abuja on Oct. 3, according to Nigeria's Centre for Disease Control, which said she is in isolation and has improved remarkably. The agency said 53 contacts had been traced. Ugandan officials are reviewing genomic sequencing, travel information, interactions and movements in coordination with Nigerian authorities and international partners. Swiss authorities had said the woman is believed to have contracted the virus in Uganda. Baryomunsi pushed back, saying Switzerland was "speaking prematurely". He said the woman's relatives from West Nile visited her in Kansanga, a suburb of Kampala, and that those relatives had visited Congo. "What evidence do they have that she never travelled there?" he said. "We should speak science, not politics." Kenya's first Ebola patient had travelled from Congo to Uganda and taken a flight from Entebbe airport to Nairobi on Oct. 3. The patient died two days later. Both the Kenyan and the Nigerian cases travelled through the same Ugandan airport on the same day but there was no physical interaction between the two, Diana Atwine, the health ministry's permanent secretary, told the press conference, citing a review of the airport's CCTV system. Baryomunsi said all 60 contacts linked to a [USN:L6N469174 TEXT:"Kenyan Ebola case"] had completed their 21-day monitoring period and been discharged. "The ministry has intensified traveller screening at Entebbe International Airport and all land border crossings. All travellers intending to enter Uganda by air, land or water must complete the passenger locator form," he said. [USN:L1N46915U TEXT:"Genomic analysis"] of Nigeria's only confirmed Ebola case showed the virus was closely related to the strain detected in Kenya's index case, though Nigerian authorities said there was no evidence that the Kenya case travelled to Nigeria or had a direct connection. Uganda borders Congo, where the outbreak began, and has previously battled Ebola outbreaks. Late on Sunday, World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said a nurse was killed and a health worker severely injured when they were attacked while responding to an Ebola alert in the northern Congolese town of Bafwasende. "Everyone working to protect communities from this deadly disease must be able to work in dignity and safety," he wrote on X, saying the attack occurred on Saturday.

Explainer-How Ukraine’s strikes on Russian energy sites deepened the rift with Trump

By Simon Lewis and Steve Holland WASHINGTON, Oct 25 (Reuters) – Relations between US President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy took a sharp downward turn in recent weeks, with each leader openly criticizing the other. The two have long had a testy relationship, but Trump’s frustration over Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure triggered a crisis that Kyiv’s supporters fear could threaten vital US support going forward.

Here’s how the relationship soured:

WHAT IS THE HISTORY OF TRUMP-ZELENSKIY TENSIONS?

Show Full Article

Trump has been skeptical of US involvement in Ukraine ever since his first term when, shortly after taking office in early 2017, he was asked to provide lethal aid to Ukraine and approved the sale of Javelin missiles to Kyiv.

“Everyone around him wanted him to do it, and they pushed him hard and he eventually signed off on selling them Javelins, very reluctantly,” said a former senior Trump administration official, who spoke on condition of anonymity. “He didn’t consider it a core US interest. It was a European issue.”

Trump’s first major encounter with Zelenskiy came in a July 2019 phone call in which the Republican president asked the Ukrainian leader to investigate his Democratic rival Joe Biden and his son Hunter, in exchange for military support Congress had authorized.

That episode led to Trump’s first impeachment. Biden beat Trump in the 2020 presidential election.

Trump also has fostered a relationship with Russian President Vladimir Putin that runs against the norms of US foreign policy but echoes his warm ties with authoritarian leaders Xi Jinping of China and North Korea’s leader Kim Jong Un.

“Trump has always wanted better relations with Russia,” the former official said.

WHAT DEEPENED THE RIFT BETWEEN THE TWO LEADERS?

Trump’s current frustration centers on Kyiv’s attacks on Russian diesel infrastructure.

Diesel prices have hit record highs since the US and Israel launched a war against Iran in February, and global energy costs spiked. US lawmakers in Trump’s Republican party face voter anger over inflation ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.

On September 13, Trump began publicly calling on Ukraine to stop targeting diesel infrastructure. The following week, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington was also concerned that Ukraine had hit US-linked oil shipments.

Ukraine has refused to halt the strikes, saying its long-range drone campaign is its only viable response to nearly five years of Russian bombardment. Moscow was forced in July to ban diesel exports as part of a raft of measures to address domestic fuel shortages.

Angered by Zelenskiy’s defiance, Trump on October 9 announced a deal to buy diesel from Moscow, issuing a temporary general license that allows Russian diesel to reach the global market. He also waived sanctions on Russia authorized by a bill he signed into law in September.

Suriya Jayanti, a former US official who runs a power sector company in Ukraine, said Russia’s strikes on Ukraine’s power grid have increased, despite Trump unilaterally announcing an energy ceasefire on October 11.

“It is clear to everyone in Kyiv that the goal is not actually an energy ceasefire, but it is really just an effort to hobble Ukraine and give Russia a decisive advantage,” said Jayanti, who is also a senior fellow at the Atlantic Council think tank.

HAS THE US THREATENED TO CUT OFF SUPPORT TO UKRAINE?

Zelenskiy has said Ukrainian military officials had been threatened by US counterparts, who said continuing the energy strikes would lead the US to cut off intelligence sharing. A US official familiar with the situation disputed Kyiv’s account.

Speaking on condition of anonymity, the US official said there has been no increase in pressure on Ukraine.

“We don’t have to pressure Zelenskiy. If he wants to make a deal he’ll make a deal. I think Putin is putting a ton of pressure on him and he (Zelenskiy) is putting some pressure on Russia but Russia doesn’t seem to be minding it as much even though they are getting hit.”

On Thursday, Trump said he had asked SpaceX CEO Elon Musk to restore Ukraine’s access to the company’s Starlink satellite system. Starlink’s disruption temporarily hampered Kyiv’s military drone operations and spurred fears that Kyiv would be left defenseless against Russia’s attacks going into the winter.

WHAT IS THE STATUS OF MOSCOW-KYIV PEACE TALKS?

Peace efforts have continued but so far have not yielded tangible results.

At talks in Oslo on October 20, Ukraine presented new proposals, and Trump’s son-in-law and envoy Jared Kushner repeated Trump’s demand that Ukraine stop attacking Russian diesel refineries.

The next day, envoy Witkoff – a close friend of Trump’s – met Putin in St. Petersburg. Putin agreed to release detained American Stephen Hubbard in what the two countries called a goodwill gesture.

Zelenskiy said on Friday that negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the US would meet in Abu Dhabi in the first half of November, a possible precursor to a meeting of the three countries’ leaders. The last US-mediated peace talks took place in February.

(Reporting by Steve Holland and Simon Lewis; Editing by Don Durfee and David Gregorio)

item.title: Trump invokes 9/11 in urging Michigan voters to oppose Muslim Senate candidate El-Sayed
item.description: Trump compared Abdul El-Sayed to the 9/11 attackers while saying Democrats would let violent anti-American terrorists into the United States.
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump at a Sunday campaign rally ratcheted up his push to link US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed to Muslim extremists, comparing him to the 9/11 attackers while saying Democrats would let violent anti-American terrorists into the United States. "I'm here to keep a jihadist, Muslim Brotherhood member from becoming a United States senator," Trump told a receptive audience in Port Huron, Michigan. If he wins, El-Sayed would be the first Muslim elected to the US Senate. Trump has sought to paint him as an anti-American Muslim radical, and on Sunday he took the rhetoric to a new level, likening El-Sayed to the attackers who took over United Flight 93 during the September 11, 2001 attacks. Michigan has one of the nation's most competitive US Senate contests going into the November 3 midterm elections, with former US Representative Mike Rogers, a Republican, and El-Sayed vying for an open seat that will help to decide control of the chamber. The president on Sunday compared voting against El-Sayed to the actions of Michigan native Todd Beamer and others who fought back against the Flight 93 hijackers. "Twenty-five years later, Michigan needs to stand up and fight, just like Todd did, to stop a jihadist from walking into the Capitol," Trump said. If El-Sayed wins, "he would be the only senator that will have to go through a metal detector before he's allowed to go in the Senate," Trump said. EL-SAYED SAYS QUESTIONING HIS LOYALTY IS 'SHAMEFUL' El-Sayed has dismissed the accusations against him and, in a recent advertisement, defended his religion, saying, "Faith is a thing there's just too little of in Washington." Rogers has alleged without evidence that El-Sayed has [USN:L6N4661FE TEXT:"ties to the Muslim Brotherhood"], one of the Arab world's oldest and most influential Islamist groups. El-Sayed has denied affiliation with the group, saying it is "shameful" for Rogers to question his allegiance to the United States. Rogers said in an interview on NBC's "Meet the Press" on Sunday, before the Port Huron rally, that El-Sayed had not sufficiently responded to questions about the allegations. "He's a Democrat Socialist of America-aligned candidate who has these pretty radical support groups that don't like America," he said. Trump's speech in eastern Michigan on Sunday came a day after former President Barack Obama campaigned for Democrats in the state, underscoring its importance in next week's elections. At Saturday's rally in Detroit, Obama framed the attacks by El-Sayed's opponents as an attempt to make him look "less patriotic and less American than they are." The former president compared them to his experience as the target of [USN:KBN23O2P2 TEXT:"false claims"] that he was born in Kenya. "We have seen this movie before," Obama said. "I starred in it ... This stuff didn't work on me. Not in Michigan. It's not going to work on Abdul." MANUFACTURING INVESTMENTS Port Huron is part of an area of Michigan that Trump won in the 2024 presidential election with more than 66% of the vote. One issue in focus during the campaign in the state has been the US-Canada tariff standoff, which has affected the Detroit-based [USN:L6N44N11O TEXT:"US auto industry"] and prompted Rogers to distance himself from the president's policy. Rogers on Sunday hailed Trump's tariffs for securing manufacturing investments for Michigan by Chevrolet and Detroit Diesel, but said "the automobile portion of these Canadian tariffs worries me a little bit." "There's some good and there's some things we have to work on," he told "Meet the Press." In a Fox News interview ahead of Sunday's rally, Trump praised Rogers as someone who shares Michigan voters' beliefs. "He's going to be an amazing senator," Trump told the "Sunday Briefing" program. "Solid as a rock. Apple pie." Democrats need to gain just a handful of seats each in the US Senate and House of Representatives to overturn Republicans' narrow 53-47 and 218-214 majorities.

item.title: バルセロナで「反体制」暴徒が略奪・放火、ブリュッセルでは警察と衝突
item.description: [バルセロナ／ブリュッセル ２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[バルセロナ／ブリュッセル ２４日 ロイター] - スペインのバルセロナで２４日夜、反体制を掲げた抗議活動の一部参加者が市中心部で店舗を略奪、路上の公共設備に放火するなど暴徒化し、約１００人が拘束された。抗議活動はソーシャルメディア（ＳＮＳ）で呼びかけられ、多くの若者が参加していた。ベルギーの首都ブリュッセルでも同日、反政府デモ隊と警察が衝突するなど、各地で混乱が続いている。

現場となったバルセロナのカタルーニャ広場は観光客や地元の買い物客でにぎわう市内有数の人気スポットで、カタルーニャ自治州の当局によると周辺の１４店舗が被害を受け、放火も３０件以上あった。拘束された人の約４分の１は未成年だという。ＳＮＳに投稿された動画には、フードを被った黒ずくめの一群が店の窓ガラスを蹴破り商品を奪って逃走する様子が映っており、一部ではオンラインの視聴者が破壊・略奪行為をあおる場面もみられた。

今回のデモは、ＳＮＳ上で「体制に反対する」運動への参加を呼びかける形で広まった。フランスで抗議活動を展開してきた学生たちを動員するために使われた「憤慨する高校生たち」というキャッチフレーズも掲げられていた。

若者を中心に数百人が抗議活動に参加したブリュッセルでは、警察に追われて転倒したデモ参加者を警察官が暴行する場面や、デモ隊が自転車や道路標識などを積み上げて火を放とうとする場面をロイター記者が目撃。別の場所では、警察が催涙ガスを使ったとの現地報道もあった。ただ、前の週に起きた衝突ほど大規模化せず、地元警察は大きな事件は発生しなかったと発表した。

item.title: Brazil's Lula takes early lead in presidential runoff vote
item.description: Corruption scandals, economic anxiety and accusations of US meddling dominated the race.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Brito, Luciana Novaes Magalhaes, Brendan O'Boyle
item.content:encoded: President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva took an early lead in Brazil's presidential runoff on Sunday evening, as results began reporting after a Supreme Court-mandated pause injected confusion into an already tight and tense runoff race. With just over 5% of tallies reported, Lula was leading right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of convicted former President Jair Bolsonaro, with around 51.16% versus Bolsonaro's 48.84%. A victory for Bolsonaro, 45, would extend a wave of right-wing victories for Latin American candidates friendly to US President Donald Trump, while a fourth mandate for Lula would be a bulwark against Washington's influence in the region as his government has pushed back on US trade and security policies. Yet the contest threatens to be overshadowed by legal disputes after Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin, who was formerly Lula's lawyer, accepted a request by Lula's campaign to extend voting, pointing to public transportation issues in three cities in the state of Bahia. Zanin's decision landed right around the election's 5 p.m. Brasilia time (2000 GMT) cutoff, creating confusion as some polling stations had already closed. In a subsequent ruling, Zanin said those stations would remain shut, allowing authorities to begin tallying those votes, but that polling stations that had not closed after the official cutoff could keep receiving voters for an additional two hours. Zanin's ruling led the electoral court, or TSE, to pause the count for two hours. PAUSE ADDS UNCERTAINTY The unexpected voting extension injects uncertainty into a Brazilian electoral process still grappling with the fallout from 2022, when Jair Bolsonaro refused to concede defeat to Lula. His supporters later invaded government buildings in protest against the result, and Bolsonaro received a 27-year prison sentence for plotting a coup. Two legal experts told Reuters the extension of voting hours and allegations around disrupted public transportation could draw legal challenges. “Depending on the election result, there is a possibility that the losing side might attempt to contest the outcome, arguing that many people were unable to vote even with the extended deadline," said Vera Chemim, a constitutional lawyer in São Paulo. The senator's brother Eduardo Bolsonaro, speaking on a live stream on his YouTube channel, questioned why the Supreme Court had ruled in a process overseen by the country's federal electoral court: "Strange, isn’t it?" he said. "It’s hard to imagine what the legal basis for this could possibly be. It doesn’t inspire credibility.” Lula had asked electoral authorities to extend voting in at least nine states after his campaign alleged some officials reduced election-day public transportation, impacting voters' ability to get to the polls. Earlier on Sunday, a court in Bahia, a Lula stronghold in the Northeast, ordered the arrest of a top transportation official in the city of Salvador over allegations that he directed a reduction in the city’s bus fleet. In comments before Zanin's decision, Lula said "something abominable is happening" in this election. Flavio Bolsonaro had also asked for voting to be extended in at least three states, citing bad weather. WASHINGTON IS WATCHING Lula and his allies see Sunday’s runoff as a chance to stem Latin America's conservative drift. Reuters on Saturday [USN:L1N4650X8 TEXT:"revealed a campaign"] within Trump's State Department to help get the Bolsonaros back in power. Trump has so far declined to endorse a candidate. Asked on Sunday who he hoped would win, Trump declined to say. "I don’t want to get into that, but we are watching," he told reporters in Washington.

item.title: ＭＬＢ＝ブルワーズがＷＳで開幕2連勝、4点差からの逆転勝ち
item.description: ［ミルウォーキー ２４日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ミルウォーキー　２４日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）は２４日、ワールドシリーズ（ＷＳ、７回戦制）の第２戦を行い、ブルワーズが地元ウィスコンシン州ミルウォーキーでレイズに５─４で逆転勝ち。対戦成績を２勝０敗とした。

ブルワーズは一回表に４点を失ったが、その裏に４番ウィリアム・コントレラス捕手と６番ギャレット・ミッチェル中堅手の適時打で２点を返した。さらに、四回に相手のエラーで１点差に迫ると、六回に８番サル・フレリック右翼手が同点ソロ。続く七回に７番クーパー・プラット遊撃手のタイムリーで逆転した。

ブルワーズは小刻みな投手リレーで二回以降、無失点。５番手で登板し、１回１／３を無安打無失点に抑えたアブナー・ウリーベ投手が勝利投手となった。

第３戦は２６日、レイズの地元フロリダ州セントピーターズバーグで行われる。これまでにＷＳで０勝２敗から逆転優勝を果たしたのは１０チームのみで、１９９６年のヤンキースが最後。

item.title: サッカー＝ドルトムントが暫定首位に浮上、バイアーが決勝ゴール
item.description: ［ドルトムント（ドイツ） ２４日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ドルトムント（ドイツ）　２４日　ロイター］ - サッカーのドイツ１部ブンデスリーガは２４日、各地で試合を行い、ドルトムントがアイントラハト・フランクフルトを１─０で下し、暫定ながら首位に浮上した。

なかなか得点が奪えず苦戦していたドルトムントだが、後半３５分にマクシミリアン・バイアーがペナルティーエリア手前から右足でネットを揺らし、これが決勝弾となった。フランクフルトの堂安律は先発し、後半４２分までプレー。同僚の小杉啓太はベンチ入りするも最後まで出場はなかった。

７試合を終えて無敗のドルトムントは勝ち点を１７に伸ばし、翌日に試合を控えるバイエルン・ミュンヘンに同３差をつけた。

佐野海舟が先発したマインツはブレーメンに２─３で黒星。佐野は後半アディショナルタイム１分までプレーした。チームメートの川崎颯太はベンチ外だった。田中聡がフル出場したシャルケはケルンとスコアドローで試合を終えた。

item.title: ＮＢＡ＝セブンティシクサーズ開幕3連勝、レブロンは欠場
item.description: ［２４日 ロイター］
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２４日　ロイター］　 -

米プロバスケットボール協会（ＮＢＡ）は２４日、各地で試合を行い、セブンティシクサーズはバックスを１２７─１１６で下し、開幕から３連勝とした。

シクサーズのジョエル・エンビードが２８得点、１１リバウンド、１０アシストでキャリア通算１０回目のトリプルダブルを記録。ジェイレン・ブラウンが２７得点、タイリース・マクシーが２６得点で貢献した。シクサーズのレブロン・ジェームズは腰の痛みを考慮して、出場メンバーを外れた。

キャバリアーズはネッツを１２５─１２１で下し、スパーズはマーベリックスに１２２─１０６で快勝。いずれも今季初勝利を挙げた。ウィザーズはトレイ・ヤングが２５得点、４リバウンド、９アシストと活躍し、ブルズを１２４─１２０で退けた。

ロケッツはホークスを１２１─１１４で下し、３勝０敗に。ヒートはホーネッツに１１０─１１５で敗れ、開幕から３試合を終えて未勝利となった。

item.title: オバマ氏、中間選挙で「愚行に歯止め」と訴え トランプ政権を痛烈批判
item.description:
Dan Catchpole
[２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Dan Catchpole

[２４日 ロイター] - 米中間選挙が来週に迫り各地で応援合戦が熱を帯びる中、接戦の中西部２州で行われた民主党の集会にオバマ元大統領が登壇した。トランプ大統領本人や政権の対イラン政策などを痛烈に批判し、中間選挙での投票は現政権の「愚行を少しでも食い止める」ための「サーキットブレーカー」であり、ブレーカーを切り替えて政府に説明責任を求めるべきだと訴えた。

ミシガン州デトロイトで上院議員候補エルサイード氏の応援に立ったオバマ氏は、トランプ氏は国民の税金で私腹を肥やし利権を売り買いする前代未聞の大統領だとし、「今や共和党は腐敗した政府、無能な政府、機能しない政府の代名詞になってしまった」と批判した。米政権が「勝利」したとしている対イラン政策では、イランがホルムズ海峡を通過する船舶の攻撃を示唆することで石油輸出国を動揺させており、結果としてイランの影響力を高めることになったと指摘した。

さらに、政権の中枢部はさまつな事柄にしか興味がなく、ヘグセス国防長官を例に挙げ「兵士の顎のラインや男性ホルモンといった『重要問題』ばかり気にしている」と皮肉り、ホワイトハウスの改装についても悪趣味だとやゆした。

ホワイトハウスはコメントの求めに即座に応じなかった。ロイターとイプソスが８月に実施した世論調査では、トランプ一族が暗号資産関連で得た収益について６３％が不適切だと回答、「大統領の政策判断は私的なビジネス上の利害関係に影響されている」との回答は６９％に上っていた。

激戦州の一つとされるミシガン州では、ピーターズ民主党上院議員の引退に伴いエルサイード候補が共和党のロジャース元下院議員と接戦を繰り広げている。オバマ氏は民主党内で依然、最も人気の高い人物の１人で、デトロイトでの集会に先立ってオハイオ州クリーブランドでも、議席奪還を目指すブラウン元上院議員の応援演説を行なった。

item.title: Aleksandar Vucic concède la défaite aux élections législatives en Serbie
item.description: Le dirigeant populiste Aleksandar Vucic a concédé la défaite aux élections législatives, alors que les Serbes se sont massivement rendu aux urnes dimanche pour chasser du pouvoir un président que nombre d'entre eux, à commencer par les étudiants qui ont multiplié les manifestations depuis deux ans, accusent de corruption.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le dirigeant populiste Aleksandar Vucic a concédé la défaite aux élections législatives, alors que les Serbes se sont massivement rendu aux urnes dimanche pour chasser du pouvoir un président que nombre d'entre eux, à commencer par les étudiants qui ont multiplié les manifestations depuis deux ans, accusent de corruption. "Nous n'avons pas encore les résultats définitifs mais (...) il est clair que nous avons perdu les élections. Le Mouvement des étudiants aura entre 135 et 140 sièges et nous en aurons 105", a-t-il déclaré. Aleksandar Vucic a démissionné de ses fonctions de président le mois dernier après avoir annoncé la tenue d'élections anticipées, dans une tentative visant à prolonger son emprise sur le pouvoir en se présentant à nouveau au poste de Premier ministre. De longues files se sont formées devant les bureaux de vote dans tout le pays, et même Aleksandar Vucic a dû patienter deux heures avant de déposer son bulletin dans l'urne. A 18h00, le taux de participation s'élevait à 67,6%, le plus élevé depuis l'éclatement de la Yougoslavie en 1992. Aleksandar Vucic a été confronté à des manifestations anti-corruption déclenchées par l'effondrement, en novembre 2024, du toit de la gare de la ville de Novi Sad, dans le nord du pays, qui a tué 16 personnes. La victoire de l'opposition estudiantine constitue un profond bouleversement politique dans ce pays des Balkans comptant quelque 6 millions d'habitants. Elle pourrait également servir de modèle à d'autres mouvements étudiants à travers l'Europe, qui sont descendus dans la rue ces dernières semaines pour protester, parfois violemment, contre la mauvaise qualité de l'enseignement et le manque de perspectives d'avenir. Depuis son accession au pouvoir en 2014, Aleksandar Vucic a supervisé une période de développement économique mais a également dû faire face à un mécontentement croissant face à ce que ses opposants qualifient de corruption et d'autoritarisme.

item.title: Ｆ１＝米国ＧＰ予選、総合優勝目前のアントネッリがＰＰ獲得
item.description: ［オースティン（米テキサス州） ２４日 ロイター］
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［オースティン（米テキサス州）　２４日　ロイター］ -

自動車レースＦ１の今季第１８戦、米国グランプリ（ＧＰ）は２４日、米テキサス州オースティンで予選を行い、総合首位のキミ・アントネッリ（イタリア、メルセデス）がポールポジション（ＰＰ）を獲得した。

２番手にはマックス・フェルスタッペン（オランダ）、３番手にはアイザック・ハジャー（フランス）とレッドブル勢が入り、シャルル・ルクレール（モナコ）が４番手、通算７回の総合優勝を誇るルイス・ハミルトン（英国）が５番手とフェラーリ勢が続いた。

同僚アントネッリとは１０２ポイント差の２位につけるジョージ・ラッセル（英国）は６番手だった。

２０歳のアントネッリは２５日の決勝で優勝し、ラッセルが９位以下、さらにハミルトンが５位以下に終わった場合、Ｆ１史上最年少王者となる。

item.title: サッカー＝バレンシア逆転負け、佐藤はベンチ入りも出番なし
item.description: ［２４日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２４日　ロイター］ - サッカーのスペイン１部は２４日、各地で試合を行い、佐藤龍之介が所属するバレンシアはビリャレアルに１─２と逆転負けを喫し、今季２勝目を逃した。

バレンシアは前半３８分にＰＫで先制。しかし追加点が奪えないまま、後半２４分に追い付かれると、同アディショナルタイム６分に逆転ゴールを許した。佐藤はベンチ入りしたものの、最後まで出番はなかった。

アトレチコ・マドリードはフリアン・アルバレスがゴールを挙げ、デポルティボを１─０で下した。エスパニョールはラシンに１─２で敗れ、エルチェはラヨ・バリェカノに３─０で白星を飾った。

１０試合を終えてアトレチコが勝ち点を２５とし、９試合消化の首位バルセロナに同２差とした。バレンシアは開幕からわずか１勝で同６の１９位と苦しんでいる。

item.title: ラグビー＝日本協会百周年記念試合、日本は男女ともに敗戦
item.description: ［２４日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２４日　ロイター］ - 日本ラグビー協会創立１００周年記念試合のリポビタンＤチャレンジカップが２４日、東京・秩父宮ラグビー場で行われ、世界ランキング９位の日本代表は同１０位のフィジー代表に２８─３４で競り負けた。

日本は斎藤直人、ワーナー・ディアンズ、マキシファウルアがトライを奪い、前半を２１─２１で折り返した。後半に勝ち越しトライを決められた後、ディアンズの２トライ目などで追い付いたものの、２本のＰＧで突き放された。

日本は９月に行われたパシフィック・ネーションズカップ決勝では、フィジーを２０─１５で下していた。日本は１１月、国際大会のネーションズ選手権のため英国に遠征し、７日にウェールズ代表、１４日にイングランド代表、２１日にスコットランド代表と対戦する予定。

この日は男女ダブルヘッダーとして行われ、世界ランキング１２位の女子日本代表は同１１位のウェールズ代表に０─１７で敗れた。

item.title: サッカー＝アストンビラがマンＣ撃破、ＧＫ鈴木が好セーブ連発
item.description: ［２４日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２４日　ロイター］ - サッカーのイングランド・プレミアリーグは２４日、各地で試合を行い、ＧＫ鈴木彩艶がフル出場したアストンビラが、開幕から７戦無敗だったマンチェスター・シティー（マンＣ）を２─１で下した。

アストンビラは前半６分に相手守備陣のミスを突いてニコラス・ジャクソンが先制弾。後半７分にアーリング・ハーランドのゴールで同点とされたが、その８分後に再びジャクソンが決めて勝ち越した。鈴木は前後半にわたって好セーブを連発。アストンビラはホームのマンＣ戦で４連勝とした。

坂元達裕が先発したコベントリーはフラムに０─１で黒星。坂元は後半４１分までプレーした。

その他、アーセナルはエバートンを２─０で下し、チェルシーはトットナムに０─２で敗れた。

８試合を終えてマンＣとアーセナルが勝ち点２１で並び、得失点差でマンＣが首位。アストンビラは同１１で暫定６位に浮上した。２勝６敗のコベントリーは同６で１９位に後退した。

item.title: ゴルフ＝バミューダ選手権、前日首位の平田は34位に後退
item.description: ［２４日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２４日　ロイター］ - 米男子ゴルフのバミューダ選手権は２４日、英領バミューダ、サウサンプトンのポートロイヤルＧＣ（パー７１）で第３ラウンドを行い、前日首位の平田憲聖は通算８アンダーの３４位に後退した。

平田は２バーディー、１ダブルボギー、５ボギーの５オーバー７６とスコアを崩し、大きく順位を落とした。１３位で出た米沢蓮も２オーバー７３と伸ばせず、通算７アンダーの４４位に後退。２アンダー６９で回った金谷拓実らと並んだ。

オースティン・スマザーマン（米国）とシェイマス・パワー（アイルランド）が通算１６アンダーの首位で並んでいる。

item.title: トランプ氏、独ＶＷの工場新設を発表 接戦ジョージア州で支持獲得狙う
item.description:
Bo Erickson David Shepardson
[ペリー（米ジョージア州） ２４日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Bo Erickson　David Shepardson

[ペリー（米ジョージア州） ２４日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は２４日、独フォルクスワーゲン傘下のアウディがジョージア州に、約４０億ドルを投じてスポーツタイプ多目的車（ＳＵＶ）を年間２０万台生産する組み立て工場を建設する計画と正式に発表した。中間選挙に向け、有権者に共和党への支持を訴える狙いがある。

同州中部のメイコン近郊ペリーで開催した政治集会で明らかにした。アウディによると、来年着工し２０３０年代初頭に生産を開始予定で、約４５００人の雇用が創出される見込み。同席したデルナー最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は「米国市場を信じているからこその長期投資だ」と述べた。

ジョージア州では１１月３日の中間選挙に向け連邦上院選と州知事選が大接戦となっており、トランプ大統領は昨年導入した自動車関税が米経済にプラスになっていると訴え支持を得たい考え。共和党の議員からは「関税がなく、常識に即した規制がなく、カリフォルニア州が燃費基準を規制する権限を撤廃していなければ、（今回の工場建設は）決して実現しなかっただろう」（バーニー・モレノ上院議員、オハイオ州選出）などと賛同する声が聞かれた。

一方で、関税が自動車価格を押し上げ、通商政策の不確実性によって自動車メーカーの一部の投資が遅れたとの批判も出ている。

米国市場向けの全車両を欧州またはメキシコから輸入しているアウディは、昨年の自動車関税導入で１２億ユーロ（薬１４億ドル）の打撃を受けた。中国での競争激化も加わり販売台数は２年連続で減少、米国販売も今年これまでに１６％減少している。

item.title: フーシ派のサウジ攻撃続く、一部再開のリヤド空港も標的と警告
item.description: [２５日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[２５日 ロイター] - イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派は２４日、サウジアラビアの石油施設や空港を再び攻撃したと発表した。フーシ派の攻撃を受けて閉鎖していたキング・ハリド国際空港の一部発着再開に対しても、引き続き同空港を「軍事目標」と見なしており利用を控えるよう改めて警告した。

フーシ派の軍事報道官は、攻撃では西部ヤンブーにある国営石油会社サウジアラムコの施設やラービグの石油精製所、原油ポンプ施設、東西パイプラインなどを標的にしたと明らかにした。いずれも、紅海沿岸に位置するサウジの主要石油・石油化学拠点。

サウジ側はフーシ派が発射した弾道ミサイル２発を迎撃し、一部の破片はメッカがある地域にも落下したと発表。これに対しフーシ派は聖地メッカとメディナへの攻撃を否定し、作戦は「サウジの石油施設と軍事基地を標的としている」と表明した。

一方、今月上旬にフーシ派の攻撃を受けて以来、閉鎖をしていたキング・ハリド国際空港は２４日夜、２つのターミナルについて発着を２５日から再開すると発表した。その数時間後、フーシ派の報道官は、空港を標的にした軍事作戦を続けるとして、全ての航空会社、空港職員、旅行者に対し利用を控えるよう改めて警告を発した。

item.title: Serbia's Vucic concedes defeat in historic election win for student protest movement
item.description: Serbia's Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat to a student-led protest movement in a historic election on Sunday that ends his long grip on power and heralds a new political era in the Balkan country.
item.dc:creator: Ivana Sekularac, Edward Mcallister, Aleksandar Vasovic
item.content:encoded: Serbia's Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat to a student-led protest movement in a historic election on Sunday that ends his long grip on power and heralds a new political era in the Balkan country. Vucic, a populist and nationalist, has dominated Serbian politics as prime minister or president since 2014. But he called snap elections in September after almost two years of student-led demonstrations against perceived corruption and creeping authoritarianism triggered by the deaths of 16 people when a train station canopy collapsed in the city of Novi Sad in 2024. "It is clear that we have lost these elections, the Student List has won," Vucic said in a televised speech. Within moments of his announcement, the streets of Belgrade erupted in celebration before the crowd swelled into the tens of thousands, with cars honking, people dancing and students shouting "victory" and "he's done". The students' win marks a profound political shift in the country of some 6 million people and is reminiscent of the defeat of Hungary's Viktor Orban in April. It may also offer a blueprint for other student movements across Europe, which have taken to the streets in recent weeks to protest, in some cases violently , against poor education standards and a lack of prospects. Vucic said the students would have between 135 and 140 seats in the 250-seat parliament and that his SNS party will have 105, based on preliminary results. "Dear Serbia, tonight the voice of the people is being heard," said Radomir Sajcic, a professor at Belgrade University, speaking on behalf of the students at their headquarters. "Tonight we celebrate victory, tomorrow we build the future." RECORD TURNOUT SPURS STUDENTS TO VICTORY Lines of unprecedented length had snaked from polling stations in cities and towns across the country earlier in the day, and even Vucic waited for nearly two hours to vote in Belgrade. Pollsters and the election commission put turnout close to 70%, the highest since the breakup of Yugoslavia in 1992. "(The turnout) did not surprise me because there was a large and strong mass that has formed throughout the past two years," said voter Katarina Petrovic. Vucic, who resigned from his second term as president to run again for prime minister, was a strong incumbent and few in the student protest movement dared believe that he would concede so fast. Supporters credit him with modernising Serbia's economy and building new highways, railways, schools and hospitals. "Some businessmen, some people will leave us but our structure is firm, we are very united, very strong, we are used to being in the opposition," Vucic said. UNCERTAINTY OVER THE STUDENTS' CANDIDATES Much remains unclear about how the student-backed candidates will fare. Their list of 250 largely unknown personalities includes university professors, actors and farmers, and is led by cardiologist Ilija Srdanovic, although it is still unclear who will be prime minister. The students' domestic agenda aims to root out graft and improve schooling. Political analysts predict some kind of purge of Vucic allies in the police, security services and ministries. But the students have been quieter on their international ambitions. As Vucic did for years, they will have to juggle relations with China, a major investor, Russia, Serbia's traditional ally and principal supplier of natural gas, and the European Union, Serbia's largest trading partner. PROTEST MOVEMENT INCREASED PRESSURE The student-led street protests sparked by the station disaster started small but quickly became the biggest in a generation, calling for Vucic to step down. Rights groups and activists say repression has worsened in the period since. "For decades the people have been waiting for this time, something to bring hope that we can live freely and by the rules of democracy," said actor Jelena Stupljanin, 48, at a Belgrade polling station. Vucic and his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) repeatedly denied accusations of repression, corruption and spying on their opponents. He said the students are funded by foreign agents in Croatia and Montenegro, a charge the students dismiss. Meanwhile, on the streets of Belgrade, a traditional brass band struck up, and a group including a man in a "students are champions" jumper floated balloons in the shape of the number 3, representing the number of the students' list of candidates. "We will drink a beer to celebrate, we will get drunk, we are so happy, I have no words to describe how much," said Andjela, a student who was with a group of friends.

item.title: Sydney's new international airport opens to passengers
item.description: Sydney's new A$5.6 billion ($3.94 billion) airport opened to passengers on Sunday after more than a decade of planning, in what Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said was a milestone for the country's most populous city.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Sydney's new A$5.6 billion ($3.94 billion) airport opened to passengers on Sunday after more than a decade of planning, in what Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said was a milestone for the country's most populous city. The new Western Sydney International Airport in Badgerys Creek, about 60 km (37.3 miles) west of central Sydney, will operate 24 hours a day, giving [USN:L1N42I00H TEXT:"airlines"] access to a fast-growing and ethnically diverse population centre. The current airport, located closer to Sydney's central business district, can host takeoffs and landings only until 11 p.m. and after 6 a.m., limiting airline scheduling options relative to other major Australian cities like Melbourne. "For the first time in more than 50 years, Australia is opening a major new airport. It’s a milestone that has been decades in the making," Albanese said in a statement. "I’m very proud to officially open it," he said. Qantas' (QAN.AX) budget arm Jetstar was due to operate the first outbound flight to the Gold Coast on Sunday, the airport said in a statement. The airport has capacity for more than 80 million passenger movements annually, it said. The start of passenger services comes after cargo flights commenced at the facility in July. Located on a 1,780-hectare (4,398-acre) site purchased by the federal government in the 1980s, the airport was completed in July 2025 after a seven-year build and 15 years of planning. ($1 = 1.4219 Australian dollars)

item.title: ゴルフ＝ＢＭＷ女子選手権、吉田が首位と4打差の2位浮上
item.description: ［２４日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２４日　ロイター］ - 米女子ゴルフのＢＭＷ女子選手権は２４日、韓国南西部・海南のパインビーチ・リンクス（パー７２）で第３ラウンドを行い、吉田優利が２位に浮上した。

６位でスタートした吉田は５バーディー、１ボギーの４アンダー６８をマーク。通算１３アンダーの２０３に伸ばし、パク・ミンジ、チェ・ヘジン（ともに韓国）と並んだ。単独首位のユ・ヘラン（韓国）とは４打差。

畑岡奈紗と岩井明愛は通算８アンダーの１９位。吉田と同じ６位で出た岩井千怜は３オーバー７５で回り、通算６アンダーの２６位に後退した。

勝みなみは通算２アンダーの４５位。古江彩佳は通算１アンダーの５４位。原英莉花と竹田麗央は通算２オーバーの７５位となった。

item.title: フィギュア＝ＧＰ第1戦フランス大会、中井亜美が2連覇達成
item.description: ［２４日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２４日　ロイター］ - フィギュアスケートのグランプリ（ＧＰ）シリーズ第１戦、フランス大会は２４日、アンジェで競技を行い、女子では中井亜美が合計２１９．７４で逆転優勝。同大会２連覇を果たした。

ショートプログラム（ＳＰ）３位だった中井は、フリーではトリプルアクセル（３回転半ジャンプ）を成功させて１位となった。ＳＰ首位の青木祐奈はフリーでは５位にとどまり、合計２００．６２点の４位。住吉りをんは合計１９０．７０点で６位だった。

男子ＳＰでは、山本草太が７７．０２点で８位。三浦佳生は７２．６７点で９位だった。アダム・シアオイムファ（フランス）が１０２．４６点で首位に立った。

item.title: Saudis say Riyadh airport partly reopens despite renewed Houthi threats
item.description: Saudi Arabia said its main airport resumed operations at two terminals on Sunday even as Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis vowed to keep striking the facility, which they called a "military target".
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Saudi Arabia said its main airport resumed operations at two terminals on Sunday even as Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis vowed to keep striking the facility, which they called a "military target". King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh had halted operations on October 10 following an attack claimed by the Houthis that killed 13 people, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade. Saudi Arabia said it intercepted another wave of missiles and drones on Sunday as fighting with the militant group continued unabated. The Houthis said they had launched attacks on the air hub among other sites in the kingdom, including in Khamis Mushait and Jazan. It was not immediately clear if those were the strikes the kingdom said it had blocked. The conflict has become an increasingly destabilising element in the US-Israeli offensive against Iran , turning US ally Saudi Arabia into a pressure point in the wider war. FLIGHT TRACKING DATA SHOWS LITTLE TRAFFIC After Saudi authorities announced the partial resumption of operations at the airport, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree vowed the facility would "never be safe" and urged airlines, airport staff and travellers not to use it. Late on Saturday, the airport said Terminal 1 would be designated for domestic flights and Terminal 2 for international flights operated by national carriers starting Sunday. Despite the announcement, flight tracking data from Flightradar24 showed little traffic at the airport on Sunday. The Saudi-led coalition said earlier this month that the Houthis had carried out 20 attacks on the airport between October 1 and 11. MISSILE AND DRONE ATTACKS CONTINUE Saudi civil defense said on Sunday that shrapnel from the interception of two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis over Khamis Mushait and Ahad Rafidah injured two people and damaged residential buildings and vehicles. Civil defense authorities earlier issued emergency alerts for Riyadh and the cities of Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jazan and Najran on Sunday, before saying minutes later that the danger had passed. The coalition said two drones and a ballistic missile were launched towards Riyadh, and a cruise missile towards the southern city of Khamis Mushait. It later said it intercepted 10 ballistic missiles fired towards southern Saudi Arabia. The Houthis said they attacked the airport and Saudi oil facilities on Saturday. Saudi authorities did not comment directly on the Houthi statements. Saudi Arabia has stepped up its strikes against the Houthis after the group seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month, closing in on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait – a global maritime chokepoint and shipping route for Gulf oil producers on the opposite side of the Arabian Peninsula to the Strait of Hormuz. The renewed fighting in Yemen has shattered a UN-brokered truce that had largely held since 2022. Saudi Arabia intervened in Yemen's civil war in 2015 at the head of a coalition supporting the internationally recognised government, after the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa a year earlier.

item.title: Inside the Trump-administration campaign to return Brazil’s Bolsonaro clan to power
item.description: Two US State Department officials pushed for sanctions aimed at tilting the election in their favor.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Stargardter
item.content:encoded: Two US State Department officials led a campaign to restore the right-wing Bolsonaro clan to power in Brazil and successfully pushed for sanctions aimed at tilting the election in their favor, according to 10 current and former US officials with direct knowledge of the matter. Their plan faces a reckoning on Sunday, when Senator Flavio Bolsonaro faces leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in a tight run-off. Lula has warned Washington against encroaching on Brazil's sovereignty and accused his opponent of plotting with the Trump administration. The two officials were Darren Beattie, a Senior Advisor for Western Hemisphere Affairs who [USN:L1N3ZM12Y TEXT:"oversees Brazil policy"], and Ricardo Pita, another senior advisor promoted this year to Deputy Assistant Secretary for North America. The details of their campaign to return the Bolsonaros to power haven't been previously reported. Beattie and Pita, both political appointees, operated with wide latitude to manage Washington's relationship with the second most-populous country in the Americas, the people said. In the months before election campaigning began, they instructed US diplomats in Brazil that it was US policy to restore former President Jair Bolsonaro as Brazil’s leader – even though he had been disqualified from office for plotting a coup in 2022, when he lost the presidential election to Lula, three of the people said. After Bolsonaro received a [USN:S0N3UJ08N TEXT:"27-year sentence in September 2025"], the two men pivoted to supporting the candidacy of his son, right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the three sources said. Beattie and Pita told embassy staff not to interact with other conservative presidential contenders who could challenge the younger Bolsonaro, they said. Since last year, the two men have successfully advocated for punitive US government measures on Brazil designed to weaken Lula and boost the Bolsonaros, the 10 people told Reuters. The policies included designating Brazilian gangs as terrorist groups and imposing US sanctions against the Brazilian Supreme Court Justice who was spearheading the investigation into Jair Bolsonaro. Reuters could not determine the extent to which the two men were acting on orders from the White House or Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Trump, a vocal defender of Bolsonaro since his election defeat in 2022, hasn’t publicly endorsed any candidate. The White House declined to comment and referred questions to the State Department. State Department Spokesman Tommy Pigott didn't answer questions about specific measures and directives involving Beattie and Pita but said in a statement: "All actions taken by the United States against narco-traffickers and to protect free speech are to defend the rights and lives of the American people. The Brazilian people have the right to choose their leaders through free and fair elections." Lula’s office did not respond to comment requests. Orna Blum, one of the officials who spoke to Reuters about Beattie and Pita’s efforts, led the State Department's Brazil and Southern Cone office until retiring last year over her opposition to the Trump administration. Washington "has every right to pursue its economic and strategic interests," she said. "But when American foreign policy instruments are used to pressure another democracy over the legal fate of a political ally, the line between diplomacy and political intervention has been crossed." SANCTIONS ON A SUPREME COURT JUSTICE Beattie is a former White House speechwriter fired in 2018 after addressing an event frequented by white nationalists. He’s also the architect of " free speech diplomacy ," a policy advocated by Trump allies that seeks to punish nations they accuse of censoring right-wing speech by US citizens, companies and global right-wing allies. The United States has accused Brazil Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes of violating free speech rights by jailing Brazilians for political social-media posts and by censoring content of US social-media companies. Moraes has argued he was ridding social media of fake news that undermined public faith in Brazil's democratic institutions. Moraes did not respond to a comment request. Pita, a conservative Venezuelan-American, is among many in Rubio's orbit who view Lula as a threat to US interests in Latin America. Rubio has been a key leader in the administration’s aggressive policy in the region, which has included an invasion of Venezuela to oust its president, an oil blockade of Cuba, and military attacks on suspected drug boats from Latin America. Beattie and Pita were drawn to the Bolsonaro family’s right-wing politics, their antipathy towards Lula, and the idea that Jair Bolsonaro was a victim of abuses by Brazil's Supreme Court. Like Trump in the 2020 US election, Bolsonaro refused to concede he lost Brazil’s 2022 presidential vote, triggering riots by supporters who stormed government buildings. The Supreme Court convicted him in September 2025 of plotting a coup to remain in power. Before the conviction, in early 2025, the Bolsonaros were aggressively lobbying Washington for sanctions under the Global Magnitsky Human Rights Accountability Act against Moraes, who had led criminal investigations into Jair Bolsonaro. The act is a 2016 federal law allowing US sanctions against foreign individuals responsible for human-rights abuses or severe corruption. Around April 2025, Jair Bolsonaro’s younger son, Eduardo, visited Beattie in his State Department office in Washington DC, according to two former US officials. Eduardo Bolsonaro had been making the public case for Magnitsky sanctions against Moraes since at least 2024, and in March 2025 he said in a livestream that it was "practically certain" the Trump administration would do so. Eduardo Bolsonaro did not respond to requests for comment. Beattie made calls to the US Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control to appeal for Magnitsky sanctions against Moraes, said a former US official with direct knowledge of the matter. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, whose department administers Magnitsky sanctions through OFAC, offered no opposition, the former official said. The US announced Magnitsky sanctions against Moraes in July 2025, citing his alleged violations of free-speech rights by censoring anti-government social-media posts. A Treasury official said Bessent and Rubio are "fully aligned on the administration’s foreign policy." TERRORIST DESIGNATIONS The Bolsonaro family was also pushing for Washington to designate Brazil's top gangs – the Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) and Comando Vermelho (CV) – as terrorist organizations. They believed such a designation would hurt Lula, who some opponents have criticized for failing to control crime. Eduardo Bolsonaro had become friends with Pita through US conservative circles, and both supported the effort to designate the gangs as terrorist groups. In May 2025, Pita joined a US delegation that visited Jair Bolsonaro at his residence in Brasilia as he awaited his trial, according to public announcements at the time. Also in the group: David Gamble, the State Department’s top sanctions official at the time. Back in Washington, Pita asked State sanctions officials to explore how terrorist designations like those [USN:S0N3ON011 TEXT:"announced against Mexican cartels"] in February 2025 could be used in Brazil, one former official said. Nearly a year later, in May 2026 – after Pita was promoted to a new job that pulled him out of Brazil affairs – presidential contender Flavio Bolsonaro met with Beattie and Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau in Washington to discuss "the urgency of designating the PCC and the Comando Vermelho as foreign terrorist organizations," according to an X post by right-wing influencer Paulo Figueiredo that included photos of the attendees. The State Department announced the designation the following day. Reuters could not determine the extent of Pita or Beattie’s influence in securing the final decision. BACKFIRES AND SETBACKS In July 2025, Washington also announced a series of other measures against Brazil, including the revocations of eight Supreme Court justices' visas and 50% tariffs on Brazilian goods, citing the "persecution" of Jair Bolsonaro. Reuters could not determine what, if any, role Beattie or Pita played in the additional measures. But if they were intended to undermine Lula, many of them backfired, according to political analysts in Brazil. Measures targeting the court did nothing to stop it from proceeding with Bolsonaro's trial, while the tariffs boosted the Lula government's poll numbers, the analysts said. Major US and Brazilian firms reliant on bilateral trade – including meatpacking giant JBS (JBSS.O) - controlled by Brazilian billionaires Wesley and Joesley Batista – also pushed back on the tariffs, which Washington eventually watered down. Beattie and Pita’s campaign also hit setbacks. Without an official explanation from the Treasury Department, the US removed Justice Moraes from the Magnitsky sanctions list in December, and in March [USN:S0N3ZG01R TEXT:"Brazil barred Beattie"] from entering the country to visit Bolsonaro in prison. Mario Braga, a Latin America analyst at risk intelligence firm RANE, said Trump may have decided to withhold a public endorsement of Bolsonaro to avoid being seen as meddling in Brazil's election – a perception that could boost Lula’s popularity. Still, after Flavio Bolsonaro narrowly outperformed Lula in the first-round election earlier this month, Trump called it a big victory. "Close, but a very, very big victory," he told reporters. "Amazing, actually."

item.title: China urges US to halt proposed expansion of outbound investment curbs
item.description: Beijing said the proposal would damage bilateral economic ties with the United States.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

China urges US to halt proposed expansion of outbound investment curbs

Beijing said the proposal would damage bilateral economic ties with the United States.

A general view of the entrance to the US Department Of The Treasury on day two of a partial government shutdown in Washington DC, Feb 1, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Ken Cedeno)

FAST

BEIJING: The Chinese commerce ministry urged the United States on Saturday (Oct 24) to stop expanding restrictions on American investments in China , saying a proposed rule on sensitive technologies would disrupt trade ties. The US Treasury Department issued proposals on Thursday to update its outbound-investment security programme , adding biotechnology to restricted sectors and expanding coverage of high-performance computing and hypersonic systems. Beijing's commerce ministry said in a statement that the proposal "discriminatorily" widened China -related investment restrictions and intensified curbs. It firmly opposed the US proposal and reserved the right to take unspecified countermeasures, it added. Beijing also said the proposal would damage bilateral economic ties and ran counter to the consensus reached by the countries' presidents, who have met twice in the past six months. The US Treasury has said the measures, which do not only cover China , are intended to stop US capital from supporting foreign adversaries' development of dual-use strategic technologies that could threaten US national security. The US programme had already restricted certain US investments involving China in semiconductors, quantum technologies and artificial intelligence.
